# מַחֲשָׁבוֹת וְהִרְהוּרִים
## מַחֲשָׁבוֹת וְהִרְהוּרִים
- Book: Eitzos HaMevuaros (Elucidated Advice)
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/shimshon-עצות-המבוארות/1/8

## English

The primary matter is to guard one's mind [לִשְׁמוֹר אֶת הַמֹּחַ] from turning sour — that is, from becoming defiled through evil reflections and evil thoughts. One must also guard one's mind from reflecting on lusts: both the lust for money — which lust overpowers every person because of a deficiency in faith in Providence — and other lusts. For reflections of lust stupefy the mind and cloud it. And through this it is impossible to pray — meaning that even when one prays, one feels no vitality or light in the prayer. And through a mind stupefied by lustful reflections, it is impossible to rejoice in any good deed or any good point. And also materially one is always dwelling in sadness and worries, G-d have mercy — because of the stupefaction of one's mind one does not feel Hashem's kindne

## Hebrew

הָעִקָּר הוּא לִשְׁמוֹר אֶת הַמֹּחַ שֶׁלֹּא יַחְמִיץ, כְּלוֹמַר, שֶׁלֹּא יִסְתָּאֵב עַל יְדֵי הִרְהוּרִים רָעִים וּמַחֲשָׁבוֹת רָעוֹת. גַּם יִשְׁמֹר מֹחוֹ מִלְּהַרְהֵר בְּתַאֲווֹת, הֵן תַּאֲוַת מָמוֹן, שֶׁתַּאֲוָה זוֹ מִתְגַּבֶּרֶת עַל כָּל אָדָם מֵחֲמַת חֶסְרוֹן אֱמוּנַת הַשְׁגָּחָה, הֵן מִתַּאֲווֹת אֲחֵרוֹת. כִּי הִרְהוּרֵי תַאֲוָה מְטַמְטֵמִים אֶת הַמֹּחַ וּמְעַכְרִים אוֹתוֹ. וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהִתְפַּלֵּל, הַיְנוּ שֶׁאֲפִלוּ כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא מִתְפַּלֵּל, אֵינוֹ חָשׁ חִיּוּת וְאוֹר בַּתְּפִלָּה. וְעַל יְדֵי מֹחַ מְטֻמְטָם מֵחֲמַת הִרְהוּרֵי תַּאֲוָה, אִי אֶפְשָׁר לִשְׂמֹחַ בְּשׁוּם מַעֲשֶׂה טוֹב וּבְשׁוּם נְקוּדָה טוֹבָה. וְגַם בְּגַשְׁמִיּוּת הוּא שָׁרוּי תָּמִיד בְּעַצְבוּת וּבִדְאָגוֹת, רַחֲמָנָא לִצְּלָן, כִּי מִשּׁוּם טִמְטוּם מֹחוֹ אֵינוֹ חָשׁ בְּחַסְדֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּר

# מַחֲלֹקֶת וּמְרִיבָה

- Book: Eitzos HaMevuaros (Elucidated Advice)

## English

One must be very careful not to become confused in the face of strife between true Tzadikim. Rather: one must believe in all the true Tzadikim, that through them it is possible to draw close to Hashem, may He be blessed, and that they conduct themselves in all matters according to the Torah and truth. For all the confusions and difficulties that arise in a person's mind regarding the true Tzadikim because of the strife between them — these flow from the mind being very corrupted through lusts and evil character traits, and especially through the corruption of the blemish of the bris — that is, evil reflections of the general lust. # מְנִיעוֹת
## מְנִיעוֹת
- Book: Eitzos HaMevuaros (Elucidated Advice)

# מִקְוֵה
## מִקְוֵה
- Book: Eitzos HaMevuaros (Elucidated Advice)
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/shimshon-עצות-המבוארות/1/11

## Hebrew

טְבִילַת מִקְוֵה מוֹשִׁיעָה מִכָּל מִינֵי צָרוֹת. הַיְנוּ, טְבִילַת מִקְוֵה לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם מְסֻגֶּלֶת לְהַצִּיל אֶת הָאָדָם מִצָּרוֹת וְיִסּוּרִים. עַל כֵּן צָרִיךְ לָדַעַת וּלְהַאֲמִין, כִּי כַּאֲשֶׁר נוֹפְלִים לְצָרוֹת אוֹ לְיִסּוּרִים חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, צָרִיךְ תֵּכֶף לָלֶכֶת לִטְבֹּל בַּמִּקְוֵה. רַק בְּוַדַּאי צְרִיכָה הַטְּבִילָה לִהְיוֹת לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם בֶּאֱמֶת וּבֶאֱמוּנָה גְּדוֹלָה. הַיְנוּ לְהַאֲמִין כִּי בִּזְכוּת קְדֻשַּׁת הַמִּקְוֵה, הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יוֹשִׁיעֵהוּ מִן הַצָּרוֹת וְהַיִּסּוּרִים, כַּמְּבֹאָר בַּפָּסוּק (יִרְמְיָה יד, ח): "מִקְוֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל מוֹשִׁיעוֹ בְּעֵת צָרָה". וּמְבֹאָר בְּסִפְרֵי אֱמֶת, כִּי פֵּרוּשׁ הַפָּסוּק הוּא, שֶׁכַּאֲשֶׁר יְהוּדִי נִזְהָר בִּטְבִילַת מִקְוֵה לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם בֶּאֱמֶת, הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מוֹשִׁיעוֹ מִכָּל מִינֵי צָרוֹת וְיִסּוּרִים.

# שַׁבָּת
## שַׁבָּת
- Book: Eitzos HaMevuaros (Elucidated Advice)
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/shimshon-עצות-המבוארות/1/13

## Hebrew

# שָׁלֹשׁ רְגָלִים
## שָׁלֹשׁ רְגָלִים
- Book: Eitzos HaMevuaros (Elucidated Advice)
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/shimshon-עצות-המבוארות/1/15

## English

Through strengthening oneself in joy on the three festivals — Pesach, Shavuos, and Sukkos — one merits the light of the countenance [אוֹר הַפָּנִים]: that is, great and true knowledge through which the holy intellect is enlivened. And through this intellect one merits the attainment of divinity [הַשָּׂגַת אֱלֹקוּת] — that is, one merits complete and genuine faith and proper fear of G-d, which are called "attainments of divinity." For through complete faith and fear one comes to know Hashem, may He be blessed, and His particular Providence as they should be. Thus is it explained in Likutay Halachos.
The primary joy is from the commandments. That is: the joy that a person rejoices in the wisdom, might, and wealth of this world is a false joy — for all the wealth of this world ends and is nul

# פֶּסַח וְחֹדֶשׁ נִיסָן
## פֶּסַח וְחֹדֶשׁ נִיסָן
- Book: Eitzos HaMevuaros (Elucidated Advice)
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/shimshon-עצות-המבוארות/1/16

## English

The days of the month of Nisan are days of repentance — just as the days of the month of Tishrei. That is: just as during Tishrei — on the days of Rosh HaShanah, Yom Kippur, Sukkos, and Shemini Atzeres — one must engage in repentance and matters of fear of G-d and Torah observance more than throughout the rest of the year, so too in Nisan one must engage in repentance and fear of G-d and Torah observance more than during the rest of the year.
Nisan is in the aspect of rectification of the bris. That is: this month is more suited for the rectification of the bris than any other time of the year — when one engages in the counsels that are effective for the rectification of the bris, as explained in the books of our Rebbe, of blessed memory. Through strengthening oneself in joy during the days of Purim — with clapping of hands and dancing — through this one merits to fulfill the commandment of counting the Omer [מִצְוַת סְפִירַת הָעֹמֶר] in completeness. And through this one merits receiving the Torah in the revealed and the concealed — that is: both in the fulfillment of the commandments that are explicitly written and explained in the Torah, and in understanding the true views that are alluded to but not explicitly stated in the Torah.

# חֹדֶשׁ אֱלוּל
## חֹדֶשׁ אֱלוּל
- Book: Eitzos HaMevuaros (Elucidated Advice)
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/shimshon-עצות-המבוארות/1/18

## English

The intention of the month of Elul is rectification of the bris. That is: through studying properly — and fulfilling the views and counsels explained in Likutay MoHaRaN Part I, §6 — how to strengthen oneself at all times and not to distance oneself from Hashem, may He be blessed: whether at the greatest ascent, or whether through the greatest fall, G-d forbid — whether materially or spiritually — these teachings are called the intentions of Elul [כַּוָּנוֹת אֱלוּל]. For all the Elul intentions explained in the writings of the Ari, of blessed memory, allude to the views and counsels mentioned above — through which one merits rectification of the bris. And through expertise in these teachings and counsels, and their genuine fulfillment, one merits to find the true match [זִוּוּג אֲמִתִּי] —

# רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה וּמִצְוַת שׁוֹפָר
## רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה וּמִצְוַת שׁוֹפָר
- Book: Eitzos HaMevuaros (Elucidated Advice)
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/shimshon-עצות-המבוארות/1/19

## English

One who hears the sounding of the shofar on Rosh HaShanah from a worthy man — one who is genuinely G-d-fearing and trembling — need certainly not worry or be afraid throughout the entire year from thunder. That is: one must trust in Hashem, may He be blessed, that in the merit of the commandment of shofar-sounding that he heard from a genuinely G-d-fearing person, Hashem will protect him from harm throughout the entire year from thunder. And as explained in Likutay MoHaRaN Part II in the Torah "Tiku Tochachah" ["Sound a reproof"] — that the shofar alludes to learning true knowledge from the true Tzadik — it is learned from this that when one hears the teaching of knowledge from a true Tzadik and a genuinely G-d-fearing person, and prevails to fulfill according to the explanation in the afo

## Hebrew

# יוֹם כִּפּוּר
## יוֹם כִּפּוּר
- Book: Eitzos HaMevuaros (Elucidated Advice)
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/shimshon-עצות-המבוארות/1/20

## English

Yom Kippur is the totality of all the days of the year [כְּלָלִיּוּת כָּל יְמוֹת הַשָּׁנָה] — for this day enlivens all the days of the year. And through the holiness of Yom Kippur the heart is rectified — that is, one's will and desires will be only for Hashem, may He be blessed. And through this all manner of strife — both materially and spiritually — is nullified, and peace is made. And through this joy flows to the person.
On Yom Kippur is the completion of the rectification of the seal of holiness [גְּמַר הַתִּקּוּן שֶׁל חוֹתָם דִּקְדֻשָּׁה] — that is, rectification of the bris. # עֵצוֹת אֲחָדוֹת
## עֵצוֹת אֲחָדוֹת
- Book: Eitzos HaMevuaros (Elucidated Advice)
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/shimshon-עצות-המבוארות/1/26

## English

Every person is obligated to know that one must not be lenient in one's mind — and must not deceive oneself — thinking that through a reflection of the lust of sexual immorality, G-d have mercy, one causes no harm. For the truth is that an evil thought is a great sin that cannot be described at all — in addition to the harm caused by it — as stated in the sacred Talmud : one must not think evil by day in order not to come to impurity at night. Therefore every person must greatly guard his thought and think only good.
Thought is in one's hand to direct wherever one wishes. For two thoughts cannot dwell in one's mind simultaneously. Therefore: if the person thinks good — or even thoughts of commerce — at that moment he cannot think evil thoughts.

 To the honor of my friend — the wondrous young Torah scholar, the veteran Chassid, the man of understanding
 [המשכיל — ha'maskil — "the one who understands, the enlightened one, the discerning scholar" — an additional honorific in this letter not present in the address of earlier letters; a mark of particular intellectual and spiritual recognition]
 — the honor of our teacher Reb Nussun, may his candle shine.
 

 
 Blessed be G-d — all of us are in the way of life and peace. May I merit to hear from you life and peace — Omain Netzach Selah Va'ed.

 [התולה ארץ על בלימה — from Job 26:7; G-d suspends the earth in the void with nothing beneath it — a striking image of absolute divine sovereignty; chosen here instead of the more common High Holiday blessing formula, drawing from the cosmic poetry of Job]
 bestow upon us a good inscription and a good sealing.

# כד
## כד
- Book: Letters of R Nosson bar Yehuda
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/nosson-by-מכתבי-ר--נתן-ב--ר-יה/1/24

## English

Tuesday, the Torah portion of Ki Tetze, the 5th of Elul, 5637
 [= late August 1877 CE — the month of Elul, the month of repentance; Rosh Hashana is less than four weeks away; the urgency of this letter is inseparable from this moment in the calendar]
 — here in Teverya.
 
[This letter is addressed to Reb Aizik — the writer's son-in-law — a different recipient from all previous letters. It is the longest and most emotionally charged letter in the collection.]
To the honor of my dear son — joined to the walls of my heart and engraved in my mind and in my spirit
 [הנצמד בקירות לבבי ונחקק במחי וברוחי — three layers of the writer's inner being: the heart, the mind (moach), and the spirit (ruach); the son-in-law is embedded in all three — bonded, engraved, present]
 — Morainu v'Rabbainu Reb Aizi

## Hebrew

ב"ה יום ג' לסדר כי תצא למלחמה ה' אלול תרל"ז פה טבריא
לכבוד בני היקר הנצמד בקירות לבבי ונחקק במחי וברוחי מו"ה איזיק נ"י עם שלום זוג' היא כלתי הצנועה והחסודה מ' קילא תח' עם שלום נכדתי מ' חיה לאנע תח' ונכדתי הנעימה מ' פיגלע תח' ונכדתי הצנועה מ' יענטא תח' ונכדי החביב והנעים מו"ה נפתלי משה נ"י ונכדי היקר וחביב מו"ה שמעון נ"י
וה' השומע טוב והמטיב הוא ייטיב לכם הכתיבה והחתימה טובה עמכם ועם בני ובנותי ובניהם ובנותיהם ועם כל אחי ואחיותי הם ובניהם עם בנותיהם וכל בעליהם ונשותיהם בטוב בכל מכל כל בתוך כלל ישראל אנס"ו
ב"ה פה אני וזוג' תח' ואמי תח' ואחותי ואנ"ש הדרים בצפת תו"ת ובירושלים תו"ת ב"ב אמן כלם בחיים ושלום כה אזכה לשמע מכם החיים והשלום ושלום דיקא והצלחה וברכה מתוך שלום אנס"ו
אחר דרישת שלומכם הטוב כמשפט באתי להודיעך ידידי בני שלא היה בדעתי לכתוב לך עוד מכתב עד אחר ר"ה הבא עלינו לטובה אך מכרח אני

# נ
## נ
- Book: Letters of R Nosson bar Yehuda
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/nosson-by-מכתבי-ר--נתן-ב--ר-יה/1/50

## English

Tuesday of the Selichos period
 [the days of penitential prayers before Rosh Hashana; this Tuesday falls in the final days of Elul, immediately before the New Year]
 — the Holy City of Teverya.
He Who stretches out the heavens like a gossamer veil
 [הנוטה כדק שמים — a direct quotation from Isaiah 40:22: "Who stretches out the heavens like a dok" — dok means a very thin, fine, transparent fabric — a gauze-veil, thinner than cloth; the heavens as a gossamer veil stretched across space]
 — may He give blessing and life — and for a good year may you be inscribed and sealed right away
 [לאלתר — le'altar — Aramaic: "immediately, right away, without delay" — the Talmudic-Aramaic word for immediacy; the blessing asks that the inscription and sealing happen without any delay]
 — for life and for go

# קט
## קט
- Book: Letters of R Nosson bar Yehuda
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/nosson-by-מכתבי-ר--נתן-ב--ר-יה/1/109

## English

Last night I received a letter from my son Aizik, may his candle shine — and within it enclosed a bill of exchange from a certain person — for he received from him from the money that he wanted — and he lent him a favor — one rendel as a free loan — so that it should arrive in my hand before Passover — so that I should have something for Passover. And now more than a month has passed — and he still has not given it to me. And he has done him a kindness — for he had nothing for the expenses of the journey to the Holy Land — and he wants to repay evil for good, G-d forbid. And in the receipt-note it is written: if he does not pay me immediately — then I have the authority to go to the local court — and they will give me a lien to the trustees — that they give me from his new monthly payment.

# קי
## קי
- Book: Letters of R Nosson bar Yehuda
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/nosson-by-מכתבי-ר--נתן-ב--ר-יה/1/110

## English

I have arrived blessed be G-d here in peace — and I had great miracles — but I have no leisure to write because of the pressures of the ship — for I cannot give counsel within my own soul — for there are two ships: one from Russia and one from Austria. The Russian ship costs two liras Francis — and the second costs more than two Turkish liras. But the Russian ship goes to Alexandria — and possibly will be two Shabboses in Istanbul. But my counsel leans toward traveling on the Austrian ship — even though I do not have so much for expenses. But Hashem Yisbarach — in the merit of Rabbainu z"l — will surely help me. And I ask of you and of all who love my soul — of the Anash — to pray for me — that He bring me across in peace to the destination of our desire — which we yearn for at all times.

ולמען ה' אחי ורעי חזקו ונתחזק בלמודי רבנו ז"ל ותלמידו הק' כי הם חיים נצחיים וחיי עולם הבא וג"ע ועין לא ראתה כי כל מה שאני לומד יותר ספריהם הק' והנוראים אני טועם טעם אחר ואלמלא לא אתינא לעלמא אלא שיהיה שם רבנו ז"ל ותלמידו הק' נקרא עלינו די כי רבנו ז"ל ותלמידו הק' רוצים להוציא כל באי עולם משבעה מדורי גיהנם ומכל הבושות שהם גרועים מהגיהנם ולהנחיל אותנו ש"י עולמות ע"י דבוריהם הק' רק אנו צריכין להפקיר את הכבוד המדמה מזה העולם ואפילו לסבל בזיונות ושפיכות דמים
כי כך אמר רבנו ז"ל שכל הצדיק הדור האמת לאמתו יש לו כח להנהיג העולם כמו שהוא יודע והצדיקים הקדמונים היה עיקר תשובתם סגופים ותעניתים ורבנו ז"ל א

# קיט
## קיט
- Book: Letters of R Nosson bar Yehuda
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/nosson-by-מכתבי-ר--נתן-ב--ר-יה/1/119

## English

Your letter from Thursday of Shemos I received properly. And because of the confusion of my mind — for my wife, may she live, her weakness has greatly intensified — with several kinds of ailments — as I wrote to you — may Hashem Yisbarach have mercy on her quickly and soon — in the merit of Rabbainu z"l and his holy disciple — in whom we take shelter — and in the merit of all the Tzaddikim who are stored away as treasure in all the cities of Judah and those stored away in the diaspora. Therefore I did not look carefully at the accounts. And now I looked at them carefully — and see — I am your good fortune [ראה אני מזלך — "see — I am your good fortune" — the writer presents himself as the recipient's mazal — his divine influence and fortune; in Kabbalistic thought the righteous intercessor

מכתבך מיום ה' שמות קבלתי לנכון ומחמת בלבול מחי שזוג' תח' חלשתה גברה עליה מאד בכמה מיני חולאת כאשר כתבתי לך השי"ת ירחם עליה חיש מהר בזכות רבנו ז"ל ותלמידו הק' שאנו חוסים בהם ובזכות כל הצדיקים הגנוזים בכל ערי יהודא והגנוזים בחו"ל ע"כ לא עינתי בהחשבונות ועכשו עינתי היטב וראה אני מזלך שלא לצדיק כל און כי אם לא היה כתב לי לא שמתי לבי לחשבון 
ולבקש כל אנ"ש שיעתירו ויתפללו עבור זוג' הכשרה רפואה ואני פורס בשלום לכל אנ"ש וגם לר' יואל צבי נ"י וקבלתי ע"י חתנו ר' יוסף הפרישת שלום שלו ולכתוב לי מר' נחמן נ"י מה הוא עשה

# קכ
## קכ
- Book: Letters of R Nosson bar Yehuda
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/nosson-by-מכתבי-ר--נתן-ב--ר-יה/1/120

## English

I am greatly astonished at you, my brother my friend — that I have no news from you about what has happened with my strong friend — the veteran Chassid Reb Nachman, may his candle shine. And also from our accounting. And also about my clothing. And you have no cause at all to be resentful against me about the letter — for my mind is very confused — from my wife's weakness — with several kinds of ailments. And she has a very high fever. And she does not taste anything at all — only broth and quinine. And she craves that someone should cook her borsht from beets [בארטט מבעריקיס — borsht fun berekes — Yiddish: borsht made from beets; borsht — the specific Eastern European beet soup; berekes — beets; the combination: the classic beet borsht she longs for and which cannot be found in Teverya] —

## English

Regarding my wife, may she live — I have much to give thanks to G-d — and I give thanks for the past and cry out for the future to Hashem Yisbarach. And know — that from several ailments Hashem Yisbarach helped her — of each of which she was in a life-threatening state. And also the fever — she did not have it from the past Monday until Shabbos. But on Shabbos — after midday — a trembling seized her again — and then the heat — but it came with mercy — relative to the previous times. May Hashem Yisbarach have mercy on her from now — for she has been left without any strength at all — and particularly on her legs — it is impossible for her to walk at all. And the magnitude of the troubles and the expansivenesses that we experienced in these four weeks is beyond all estimate and reckoning. Fo

# קכד
## קכד
- Book: Letters of R Nosson bar Yehuda
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/nosson-by-מכתבי-ר--נתן-ב--ר-יה/1/124

## English

I am informing you — that my wife, may she live, is still not fully in good health. The fever — blessed be G-d — has departed. But the harsh cough has not departed at all — and because of this all her limbs have become disjointed and unhinged — and it is impossible for her to regain her strength. And furthermore — since last Friday — a severe eye pain has intensified upon her — at first with very great heaviness — but now blessed be G-d it has eased a little — blessed be G-d, blessed be G-d.
My brother, my friend — it is impossible to tell you my intense suffering — only blessed be G-d that we know of Rabbainu z"l and his holy disciple — they give me life in all the troubles that pass over me now. And beyond this — I do not know from where one receives life-force — only that there is a kin

## קכז
- Book: Letters of R Nosson bar Yehuda
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/nosson-by-מכתבי-ר--נתן-ב--ר-יה/1/127

## English

In the past week I wrote you a letter — but the wagon did not arrive — and my sister received it — and went to the gate — and encountered a certain man — and gave him the letter. And now it has become known to me that this man stole from our friend Reb Chaim Yehoshua, may his candle shine — and surely he did not deliver the letter.
And now I write to you — how Hashem Yisbarach exercises divine providential oversight over me: when Hashem Yisbarach helped me with my wife, may she live — and Hashem Yisbarach healed her completely — in the merit of Rabbainu z"l and in the merit of your prayers — today she went to my sister, may she live — and on the way back she fell upon a stone — and it was a miracle that she did not break her head, G-d forbid, and all her limbs — for she remained weakened.

## English

I bring you a good tiding — that your brother-in-law Morainu v'Rabbainu David, may his candle shine — has been saved from the standing obligation — and he has remained in Krizrad. For on the eve of Passover I received a letter from my son Moshe Efraim, may his candle shine — from the Torah portion of Tetzaveh — and within it enclosed was a letter from your brother-in-law Morainu v'Rabbainu Nussun, may his candle shine — and there it is written that your co-parent-in-law, may his candle shine, is in Tcheryn. And throughout the intermediate days of the festival — there was no wagon to send you the letter. - Book: Letters of R Nosson bar Yehuda

## English

And what shall we do about the dangerous ordeals [הרפתקאות — harpatka'os — Talmudic Aramaic: dangerous encounters, perilous adventures along the way; from Aramaic riftaka — a dangerous encounter; used in the Talmud for harrowing ordeals on a journey] that have passed over us — everything is from Hashem Yisbarach — and surely He brings forward the remedy before the affliction. We need only to incline ourselves toward the hints that Hashem Yisbarach hints to us — and not despair of mercy. For Hashem Yisbarach tests us at all times — for this world is the world of trial.

For the sake of Hashem — tell our friend Reb Dov, may his candle shine — not to be hasty in selling the pillows and cushions. And the essential thing for us is to renew ourselves in prayer — for all the business of Rabbainu

## English

For Hashem Yisbarach knows — that I love each and every one of the Anash — and I judge each and every one favorably — as Rabbainu z"l desired. And our matter is sustained by affection. And because of the troubles that were filled with expansivenesses — my mind was confused — to write to you letters at every occasion. And G-d willing when Hashem Yisbarach helps and gives a complete healing to my wife, may she live — surely G-d willing my strength will be renewed — to write to you letters at every occasion. For blessed be G-d — in our business — there is much, much to speak about — and to arouse each person his companion.

## English

And I ask still more — of all the Anash — to pray for my wife, may she live — for she again has the fever — very strong. And she has no strength at all to bear it — for these are four months during which every day her weakness grows stronger. And beyond this — she has several ailments — and she cannot eat — not even like a newborn infant of one day. [כתינוק בן יומו — "like a newborn infant of one day" — the Talmudic phrase for the most minimal possible: even a newborn infant of one day eats something; she cannot manage even that] May Hashem Yisbarach have mercy on her — together with the other sick of His people Israel — in the merit of all the Tzaddikim — and in the merit of Rabbainu ז"ל. And may He receive our prayers quickly and soon — on behalf of all Israel. Words of one who truly lov

## English

Your letter — with the whiskey — I received properly. And thank you — for the counsel from you — that you did not send the pillows and cushions — for I was very much afraid of imposing upon our friend Reb Dov, may his candle shine. Only — because there was no other option — because of the poverty of my home — I had no other way. And "Cast your burden upon Hashem." [Psalms 55:23 — "Cast your burden upon Hashem and He will sustain you" — hashlich al Hashem yehavecha; the verse of complete trust in casting one's load upon G-d] But now that Reb Yosef is traveling — it is surely better to send them with him.

## English

Therefore I thought within my mind — that we have no counsel and no stratagem — except prayer and supplication — as per the will of Rabbainu ז"ל and his holy disciple. But "a prisoner cannot release himself" [Babylonian Talmud, Berachos 5b — "a prisoner cannot release himself from his prison" — one cannot pray for oneself out of one's own constriction; one needs the prayers of others; the writer applies this to his wife's illness — he needs the prayers of the Anash] — etc. Therefore I ask of all the Anash — our truly beloved — to pray for her — with mercy and supplication — that Hashem Yisbarach send her a complete healing quickly and soon — together with the other sick of His people Israel. ## English

On Wednesday, Reb Altir, may his candle shine, came here — and told me that he has a letter from you for my hand — and told me orally that your precious son is ill with the fever-ailment. And the letter was lost with him. And immediately I went with my wife, may she live, to the graves of the Tzaddikim from our land — namely Reb Nachman and Reb Mendele and Reb Avraham Kalisker — and other Tzaddikim — may their merit protect us. And I performed a redemption for him — from my own gift-money — and also today I prayed for him. May Hashem Yisbarach hear my prayer and send him a complete healing — in the merit of all the Tzaddikim — and in the merit of Rabbainu z"l and his holy disciple. ## English

Praise to G-d — blessed be G-d, blessed be G-d — here all of us are in the line of life and peace. So may I merit to hear from you — life and peace and a complete healing — together with all of Israel — without limit.
On Wednesday, Reb Altir, may his candle shine, came here — who is traveling to Jerusalem — and conveyed to me greetings of peace from you — and told me that your precious son is not in good health. And he had a letter from you — but he lost it. And immediately I came home and told my wife, may she live, and my sister, may she live — and immediately went with them to the graves of the Tzaddikim — and performed a redemption from my own money — which I gave as a gift for your son. - Book: Letters of R Nosson bar Yehuda
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/nosson-by-מכתבי-ר--נתן-ב--ר-יה/1/136

## English

I am very, very astonished — that you have withheld the fruit of your pen — not to inform me about your son, may his candle shine. For we had news at the time that you wrote to me with Reb Altir — that your son, may his candle shine, is ill, G-d have mercy — but he did not give me the letter — for it was lost with him — only orally he told me. And immediately I and my wife and my sister, may she live, went to the holy resting places — and I gave from my own money as a gift — a redemption for him. And I wrote to you two letters after this — and in the end we have no news at all. And the magnitude of the anguish of our soul is beyond all estimate and reckoning — for our eyes are consumed with watching. # קלח
## קלח
- Book: Letters of R Nosson bar Yehuda
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/nosson-by-מכתבי-ר--נתן-ב--ר-יה/1/138

## English

We hereby inform you — that I received your letter properly today. And Hashem Yisbarach give you life — in all good — as your soul desires — and as per His good will — as I want to see in you. Just as you gave me life with your letter — with the good news of the health of your precious son — for nearly our breath had been cut off from extraneous thoughts [מחשבות זרות — machshavos zaros — "extraneous thoughts" — in Breslov teaching, foreign and alien thoughts that invade the mind unbidden; here used to mean fears and anxious imaginings about the worst; the writer's mind had been seized by these alien fearful thoughts] — may Hashem Yisbarach lengthen his days and years — and give you children — a seed that endures — in this very year. May Hashem Yisbarach add upon you and upon your children.

- Book: Letters of R Nosson bar Yehuda
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/nosson-by-מכתבי-ר--נתן-ב--ר-יה/1/159

## English

I am astonished — on Sunday of Tetzaveh I wrote a letter to the honor of Reb Yaakov Ber, may his candle shine — and the letter was delayed — and I did not send the letter until the above-mentioned Friday. And I sent it through the hired coachman Mohamad Salach the blind one. [The same hired coachman referred to in Letter 159 — the blind coachman Salach who regularly carried letters between Teverya and Tzfas; his blindness is mentioned as a distinguishing characteristic] And there I wrote to you that you should send me immediately the above-mentioned matter that I wrote to you on Sunday of Tetzaveh — for it was a precious letter to give life to your souls. And the hired coachman was with us in the past week several times — and he told me that upon his coming he returned your letter to you.

Your letter I received on Friday — the eve of Shabbos — after midday. And I had no leisure at all to reply to you as befits replying to two such beloved ones. Only I wrote you a receipt for your letter. To Reb Dov — two groshen. To Reb Itzig — two groshen. To Reb Aizik — two groshen. And to the widow of Reb Itzele — one groshen. ## English

I hereby inform you — that I am laid low in weakness — with fever and constipation [חמימות ועצירות — "heat and constipation" — chimimus — fever, heat; atzirus — constipation, obstruction; a combination of acute symptoms that has left the writer bedridden for a week] — for seven days. Therefore — pray for me — to Hashem Yisbarach — in the power and merit of Rabbainu ז"ל and his holy disciple — and in the merit of all the Tzaddikim — that Hashem Yisbarach send me quickly and soon —

## English

§ 1
 Alef — The Letter Alef
 א

ALEF — Numerical Value: 1 | 114 source entries

 [Translator's Note] The entries begin with the letter Alef itself — its shape, hidden form, and components — then proceed alphabetically through all Hebrew words beginning with Alef. Every entry records a mystical connection taught by Rebbe Nachman. Hebrew is always shown alongside the English. Cross-references (where the same connection appears listed from both directions) are presented as single unified entries.

 
 Hebrew Entry
 English Translation & Explanation
 Source
 

 א
 
 Shape / Form

 The letter Alef (א) embodies three components: an upper point, a lower point, and a Vov (ו) between them. In this way the Alef carries the visual form of the letters ר׳י׳ו׳ — Reish-Yud-Vov — whose numerical value is 2

## English

§ 2
 Bais — The Letter Bais
 ב

ב

BAIS — Numerical Value: 2 | First letter of the Torah | 52 source entries

 [Translator's Note] The letter Bais begins the Torah (Bereishis — "In the beginning") and carries the significance of blessing (berachah) and of the revealed, created world. Many entries in this section revolve around the word Bereishis itself and its multiple permutations. Cross-references (the same connection listed from both directions in the source) are consolidated into single entries.

 
 Hebrew Entry
 English Translation & Explanation
 Source
 

 ב׳ ראשית
 
 Notarikon

 The word Bereishis (בראשית, "In the beginning") is read as ב׳ ראשית — "Bais is the beginning." The Torah begins with Bais because Bais is the letter of berachah (blessing) and of the revealed world.
 
 Likut

## English

ג

GIMEL — Numerical Value: 3 | 9 source entries

 [Translator's Note] Gimel is the smallest section in the work — relatively few key terms in Rebbe Nachman's teachings begin with this letter. The standout entry is the dreidel teaching, which reveals the four Chanukah letters encoded in a verse of redemption from Psalms. Note that source lines 1–2 are a single entry (the citation was split across two lines in the original).

# אוֹת ו'
## אוֹת ו'
- Book: Kuntres HaTzerufim (Pamphlet of Combinations)

## English

ו

VOV — Numerical Value: 6 | The letter of connection and extension | 40 source entries

 [Translator's Note] The letter Vov is the Hebrew letter of connection — the word vov itself means "hook" or "peg," and as a prefix it means "and." Grammatically it joins clauses; spiritually it connects upper and lower worlds. Many entries here reflect that connecting, extending quality. Cross-references consolidated throughout.

 Hebrew EntryEnglish Translation & ExplanationSource

 ו — name contains a ו
 
 Notarikon

 The letter Vov (ו) cannot be pronounced without a second Vov — for its name is spelled ואו (Vov-Alef-Vov), which contains another Vov within it.
 [Like Alef (which cannot be pronounced without Peh), the Vov contains its own name within itself — it is self-referential, a letter whose n

## Hebrew

וַיַּפֵּל רָאשֵׁי תֵבוֹת פֶּה לָהֶם וְלֹא יְדַבֵּרוּ. [ליקו"מ י"ט]
וְרִידִין אוֹתִיּוֹת רי"ו די"ן, הוּא שֵׁם אֲדֹנָ"י, כִּי רי"ו הוּא צוּרַת אָלֶף וְכוּ'. [ליקו"מ ל"ז] 
וַיִּבֶן רָאשֵׁי תֵבוֹת וּתְקַעְתִּיו יָתֵד בְּמָקוֹם נֶאֱמָן. [ליקו"מ ח"ב א']
וְרַפֹּא יְרַפֵּא עִם הַשְּׁנֵי תֵבוֹת בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא פִּדְיוֹן נָפֶשׁ. [ליקו"מ ח"ב ג']

וַיִּבְאַשׁ רָאשֵׁי תֵבוֹת שָׂרָה אֶסְתֵּר בַּת יְהוּדִית וַי וּמֵתָה. [שיחות הר"ן בסופו]

 Hebrew EntryEnglish Translation & ExplanationSource

 ז׳ שמות
 
 Gematria

 The seven Divine Names — ע"ב, ס"ג, מ"ה, ב"ן, קס"א, קנ"א, קמ"ג (72, 63, 45, 52, 161, 151, 143) — together have the gematria of 686 (תרפ"ו) lights.
 [These seven Names correspond to the seven spellings of the four-letter Divine Name, each using different vowel-letters. Their sum (72+63+45+52+161+151+143 = 687... the source reads 686 using a specific calculation variant) represents the full spectrum of divine light.]

## English

י

YUD — Numerical Value: 10 | Smallest letter, point of all beginnings | 62 source entries

 [Translator's Note] The Yud is the first letter of the Divine Name and the smallest letter in the alphabet — a single point that contains infinite potential. Source lines 19–20 and 33–34 are each one entry split across two lines. Cross-references to earlier sections are noted and consolidated.

Hebrew EntryEnglish Translation & ExplanationSource

 י׳ × 7
 
 Gematria

 The letter Yud seven times (7 × 10 = 70) = the gematria of ע׳ (Ayin, the letter whose numerical value is 70). Seven Yuds = one Ayin — the divine point multiplied seven times becomes the eye of wisdom.
 
 Likutay Mooharan 94

 י׳, י"ק, יק"ו, יקו"ק
 
 Gematria

 The four progressive expansions of the Divine Name — י׳ (10), י"ק (20), יק

## English

כ

KAF — Numerical Value: 20 | The letter of the palm, of potential, of the crown | 33 source entries

Hebrew EntryEnglish Translation & ExplanationSource

 כ׳ — requires פ׳
 
 Notarikon

 The letter Kaf (כ) cannot be pronounced without the letter Peh (פ) — for its name is Kaf, which contains Peh. [Part of the six-letter cluster requiring Peh — cross-reference from Section 1.]
 
 Likutay Mooharan 83

 כ׳ = יוד
 
 Gematria

 The letter Kaf (= 20) = gematria of Yud spelled out (יוד = 10+6+4 = 20). The Kaf is the Yud fully spelled — the potential of the point fully extended. [Cross-reference from Section 10.]
 
 Likutay Mooharan II:82

 כוס
 
 Gematria

 Kos (כוס, "cup" = 86) = gematria of Elokim (86). [Cross-reference from Section 1.]
 
 Chayay Mooharan §577

 כוסי
 
 Roshay Saveivos

 Kosi

כַּלֹּת רָאשֵׁי תֵבוֹת כַּפָּרָה לְכָל תּוֹלְדוֹתָם. [ליקו"מ קנ"א]

## אוֹת ל'
- Book: Kuntres HaTzerufim (Pamphlet of Combinations)

## English

ל

LAMED — Numerical Value: 30 | The tallest letter, reaching upward | 22 source entries

Hebrew EntryEnglish Translation & ExplanationSource

 ל'א ת'בערו א'ש ב'כל מ'ושבותיכם
 
 Roshay Saveivos

 The first letters of "You shall not kindle fire in any of your dwellings [on Shabbos]" (ל׳א ת׳בערו א׳ש ב׳כל מ׳ושבותיכם) [Exodus 35:3] spell מתאבל (mis'abel, "one who mourns"). The prohibition of fire on Shabbos encodes mourning — for on Shabbos the fires of judgment are extinguished, and those who violate it mourn their loss.
 
 Likutay Mooharan II:67

 לב — ב׳ראשית…ישראל׳
 
 Tziroof

 Lev (לב, "heart") = the first letter of the Torah (ב of בראשית) and the last letter of the Torah (ל of ישראל). The Torah from beginning to end is the heart. [Cross-reference from Section 2.]

 Roshay Saveivos

 Lev

צָרָה לָשׁוֹן צוּרָה. [ליקו"מ ק"ע]

Hebrew EntryEnglish Translation & ExplanationSource

 ק — from ה׳
 
 Shape / Form

 The letter Kuf (ק) is formed when the leg of the Heh (ה) is lengthened downward. [Cross-reference from Section 5.] The divine letter of revelation (Heh) extends its reach into the lower worlds to become Kuf.
 
 Likutay Mooharan 67:4

 ק — requires פ׳
 
 Notarikon

 The letter Kuf cannot be pronounced without the letter Peh — its name (Kuf) contains a Peh. [Part of the six-letter cluster, cross-reference from Section 1.]
 
 Likutay Mooharan 83

 קבלה
 
 Gematria

 Kabbalah (קבלה, "mystical tradition / receiving" = 137) = gematria of no'af (נואף, "licentiousness" = 137). [Cross-reference from Section 14.] Same ch

# הקדמה
## הקדמה
- Book: Kuntres HaTzerufim with Completions
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/nosson-by-קונטרס-הצירופים-עם-ה/1/2

## English

Translated in merit of Na Nach Nachma Nachman MayUman — נ נח נחמ נחמן מאומן
Section 2 of 22 — complete

## Hebrew

מבעל קונטרס הצרופים הראשון
אני העני ואביון, החסר משכל זך וצח ומן רעיונים זכים וטהורים להשיג בזכרון במוחי כל דבור ודבור מאמרות טהורות כסף צרוף מזוקק שבעתים מעריבות נעימות מתיקות ידידות מספרי רבינו, הנחל נובע מקור חכמה, אשר נועם שמו המתיק בזה הפסוק (א). אור תורתו מאיר בכל העולמות, והוא התחיל בתיקון הכללי ויגמור (ב).
ואני שמעתי מתלמידו הקדוש אשר סמך ידיו גלילי זהב טהור עליו, אשר מה שנאמר בדברי חכמינו זכרונם לברכה (ג). "אשרי מי שבא לכאן ותלמודו בידו" נאמר עתה על ספרי רבנו הקדוש זצוק"ל, כי רבינו ז"ל אמר (ד) שבכל תורה ותורה כלול כל דברי תורה שבכתב ושבעל, פה, והם שרשי התורה. אמרתי בלבי, לפי קט שכלי זה אצלי בלתי אפשר כי הם עמוקים מאד מני ים, ובכל תורה ותורה נמצא כללים ופרטים וענינים רבים וסודות גדולות, על, כן יישבתי בדעתי, אם אינני יכול לעשות כלא מצוה על כל פנים אעביד חלק מהמצוה, ואציגה כל הצירופי

---

## English

ZAYIN — Numerical Value: 7 | The letter of the seventh, of Shabbos, of completion | 8 source entries

Hebrew Entry English Translation & Explanation Source

ז׳ שמות Gematria The seven Divine Names — ע"ב, ס"ג, מ"ה, ב"ן, קס"א, קנ"א, קמ"ג (72, 63, 45, 52, 161, 151, 143) — together have the gematria of 686 ( תרפ"ו ) lights. [These seven Names correspond to the seven spellings of the four-letter Divine Name, each using different vowel-letters. Their sum (72+63+45+52+161+151+143 = 687... the source reads 686 using a specific calculation variant) represents the full spectrum of divine light.] Likutay Mooharan 2:2

זיעה / ז'ה ה'יום ע'שה י'י Roshay Saveivos Zeiah ( זיעה , "perspiration / sweat") — its letters are the first letters of ז׳ה ה׳יום ע׳שה י׳י : "This is the day that Hashem has made" [Psal

# כ
## כ
- Book: Kuntres HaTzerufim with Completions
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/nosson-by-קונטרס-הצירופים-עם-ה/1/13

## English

KAF — Numerical Value: 20 | The letter of the palm, of potential, of the crown | 33 source entries
Hebrew Entry English Translation & Explanation Source
כ׳ — requires פ׳ Notarikon The letter Kaf ( כ ) cannot be pronounced without the letter Peh ( פ ) — for its name is Kaf , which contains Peh . [Part of the six-letter cluster requiring Peh — cross-reference from Section 1.] Likutay Mooharan 83
כ׳ = יוד Gematria The letter Kaf (= 20) = gematria of Yud spelled out ( יוד = 10+6+4 = 20). The Kaf is the Yud fully spelled — the potential of the point fully extended. [Cross-reference from Section 10.] Likutay Mooharan II:82
כוס Gematria Kos ( כוס , "cup" = 86) = gematria of Elokim (86). [Cross-reference from Section 1.] Chayay Mooharan §577
כוסי Roshay Saveivos Kosi ( כוסי , "my cup") — first let

Reb Leibele Konstantiner was the cantor in Uman on Rosh HaShanah in the days of Reb Nachman of Tulchin. The story of how it came about was thus: Reb Leibele lived in the city of old Konstantin [which is far from Uman] and was the cantor there — and therefore could not come to Uman for Rosh HaShanah. He would draw people close to Rabbainu and send them to Uman for Rosh HaShanah, while he himself would remain there as described. In the course of time he merited to draw close a man named Reb Ayzikl [who afterward lived in Uman]. When Rosh HaShanah drew near, Reb Ayzikl said to him: "If you are not traveling — then neither am I traveling." - Book: Stories of R Moshe Glidman

## English

There was a story of two poor women in the same city. One was a follower of Moharan'as and the other of the Savraner. The one who followed the Savraner said: "You receive more from Moharan'as than I receive from my Rebbe. For when I come to my Rebbe and list all my needs at the beginning of winter — he gives me part but not everything. But you — when you go to Moharan'as, he shows you that nothing is lacking for you at all. And so you have more than I do."
Rabbainu said: "I want" — and one must say "I agree" — "that you speak of me and do not mention my name. It does not bother me if someone recites Grace after meals with devotion and this flows from my power — and he does not know it flows from my power."

## English

A story concerning the holy Tzaddik Reb Nachman of Horodenka, of blessed memory — the grandfather of our holy Rabbainu — who was one of the great disciples of the holy Ba'al Shem Tov and was literally the manager of the Ba'al Shem Tov's household. All the keys of the Ba'al Shem Tov's house were in his possession, as is well known.

Reb Nachman had a sister in some town (seemingly in Horodenka). Once he came with the holy Ba'al Shem Tov and they lodged in her home. The Ba'al Shem Tov had a long pipe reaching down to the ground, and he packed the pipe with tobacco. When he needed to light the pipe, Reb Nachman took a live coal and stretched himself out fully — prostrating with outstretched hands and feet — and extended the pipe to light it.

# ד)
## ד)
- Book: Stories from R Shmuel Horowitz
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/stories-סיפורים-מר--שמואל-הו/1/4

## English

Michoel son of Reb Arkes, from the grandchildren of Rabbainu (who was related by marriage to the family of Reb Shneur Zalman of Liadi) — how he became somewhat elevated in status and wealth, and Moharan'as perceived in him a trace of haughtiness. Moharan'as rebuked him and said: "Do you think that when King David, peace be upon him, cried before the Almighty 'Save me from the mire and let me not sink' — he was at a low spiritual level? He was a king like all kings, who ruled over other kings. He walked in royal garments with kingly dignity, the royal orchestra played for him, and princes and ministers surrounded him — and from that very exalted place he cried: 'Save me from the mire and let me not sink.'"

## English

One of our fellowship answered him with a parable: A man once entered a house and stood upside down — head below and feet above — and cried out that the whole house and everything in it was upside down. A sensible man came and told him: "The house is not upside down — you are upside down. Right yourself and you will see that everything in the house is perfectly straight." And then he said to the questioner: "Dayn moykh iz iberkert — dukht zikh dir az alts iz iberkert. Zloakh dayn moykh — vet als zayn gleykh." - URL: https://ajew.org/reader/stories-סיפורים-מר--שמואל-הו/1/7

## English

Concerning Reb Ephraim son of Reb Naftali, a disciple of Rabbainu. When he was traveling from Uman to the Holy Land, a philosopher came along the road and pressed him with philosophical challenges, confusing his mind on Shabbos. He replied that he had no time for this now — let the man come on motzei Shabbos and he would answer everything with a single answer.

On motzei Shabbos the philosopher came at the very moment Reb Ephraim was holding the cup to recite Havdalah. Reb Ephraim called him over and said: "In the holy Torah and the holy Zohar it is prophesied that there is a gehinnom called Sha'ol. Now one might ask: why is it called Sha'ol? The answer is: this gehinnom is for those who question and investigate — they lift his shirt and flog him and say to him: 'Sha'ol!' [You asked! You i

## English

A story concerning Rabbainu who commanded his sister Perel to divorce her husband — his brother-in-law. He said of him: "Er iz a nar" [He is a fool] — "Az er iz a nar, nart im der Ba'al Din in Yidishkeit azoy" [Being a fool, the Accuser misleads him in his Yiddishkeit in this way].

Regarding the birth of Rabbainu — it is already explained in what was recorded above how Reb Simcha was on the road and became lost, and how his wife Feiga had distress and searched for him in all she did to honor the Shabbos and could not find him. She was in very great distress. # א)
## א)
- Book: Stories from R Shmuel Horowitz
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/stories-סיפורים-מר--שמואל-הו/1/9

## English

They told before the son of the holy Tzaddik Reb Pinchas of Koritz about the controversy of the Elder [the Shpole Zeide] against Rabbainu. He asked: "What does Rabbainu say?" They answered: he is silent. He replied: "Now a Mishnah in Avos is resolved for me. It says there: 'What is a controversy not for Heaven's sake? The controversy of Korach and his assembly.' Why does it not say: 'The controversy of Korach and Moshe'? The reason is: Moshe did not contest at all — he was simply silent. Only Korach and his assembly were the ones contesting. And so it is here: Rabbainu does not contest — only they are contesting, and he is silent."

## English

The Rav, the Gaon, Reb Tzaddok of Lublin sought Rabbainu's books very greatly, and commanded all booksellers that the moment any of Rabbainu's books came to hand they should bring them to him immediately. He would lament: "When a book comes out, one catches them — by the time you notice, there are no more copies." ("Az es kumt aroys a bukh — khap men sey, az ts'merkumt, iz nito kayn sefer.")

Once he found a book vendor and asked if he had any Breslov books. The vendor said he had none. Nonetheless Reb Tzaddok searched his stock and found the book Alim LeTrufah — the letters of Moharan'as. He asked what it was. The vendor replied: "Only a letter-writer [brifshetler]." Reb Tzaddok answered: "Precisely this letter-writer is what I want!" He immediately read the first letter — which describes

# י)
## י)
- Book: Stories from R Shmuel Horowitz
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/stories-סיפורים-מר--שמואל-הו/1/11

## English

The renowned Gaon Reb Gershon Henich of Radzimin — author of the Techeiles — was in Uman at Rabbainu's holy grave and said that it was now resolved for him why people do not travel and the Tzaddikim do not gather at Rabbainu's grave. Because Rabbainu shows the great ones that there is still "no place of His glory" in their attainment — that they are still below and have not yet grasped anything — and he humbles them. Therefore they do not travel and draw close, for who wants to be humbled? But to the small ones he shows that "the whole earth is full of His glory" — that there is still hope for them — and he elevates them. Therefore they travel and draw close.

## Hebrew

הרב הגאון מוה"ר צדוק מלובלין הי' מחפש מאד את ספרי רבינו ז"ל והי' מצוה לכל המוכרי ספרים שתיכף שיזדמן להם ספרי רבינו שיביאו אליו והי' מתאונן ואומר שכשיוצא אין הספרים איך האם שוין אזא גליק ציא חאפט מען זייא אז ציאמירקואט ניטאן קיין ספר. ופ"א מצא מוס' ושאלו אם יש לו ספר מספרי ברסלב וענה לו שאין לו ואעפי"כ חיפש אצלו ומצא הס' עלים לתרופה מהמכתבים של מהרנ"ת ושאלו מה זה ענה זה רק בריף שטעליר ענה ר' צדוק ואמר דווקא זה הבריף שטעליר אני רוצה ותיכף שקרא המכתב הראשון שכתוב בו מהרדיפות שרדפו את מהרנ"ת הוריד דמעות ע"ז:

# יא)
## יא)
- Book: Stories from R Shmuel Horowitz
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/stories-סיפורים-מר--שמואל-הו/1/12

## English

Rabbainu said in Yiddish: "Mayni layt veln zikh gefunen viya kayn mentshin gayen nit, un viya kayn heyner krayen nit" [My people will find one another in a place where no people walk and where no rooster crows] — meaning: they will be in places of hisbodedus and night-waking, in utter solitude.

# יב)
## יב)
- Book: Stories from R Shmuel Horowitz
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/stories-סיפורים-מר--שמואל-הו/1/13

## English

Rabbainu said: "Azmen po'elt nor mit gutn — un az es dukht zikh azmen hot mit baysn ku gep'oylt, zol men visn az mit gutn volt men asakh mer gep'oylt" [One accomplishes only with goodness — and if it seems that one accomplished something through harshness, one should know that through goodness one would have accomplished far more].

## Hebrew

רבינו ז"ל אמר ייני לייט וועלין זיך גפונין וויא קיין מענטשין גייאין ניט, אין וויא קיין היינער קרייאין מט. היינו שיהי' להם התבודדות והנעור בלילה.

# יג)
## יג)
- Book: Stories from R Shmuel Horowitz
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/stories-סיפורים-מר--שמואל-הו/1/14

## English

During the controversy of the rabbi of Savran against Moharan'as — when they oppressed him greatly — Moharan'as answered and said: "Fun mir vet blaybn a shank [migdal] mit sforim — un fun zey vet blaybn a shank mit flesher" [From me will remain a tower of books — and from him will remain a tower of bottles]. And so it came to pass: from Moharan'as there remained a tower full of manuscripts — all of the Likutay Halachos and so forth. And from the other nothing remained except a tower with bottles — for he had been ill and drank wine continually, and a tower full of bottles remained — as is well known to all.

## Hebrew

רבינו ז"ל אמר, אזמען פועלט נאר מיט גיטין, אין אז ע"ס דווכט זיך אזמען האט מיט בייזין כוא גפועלט זוול מען ווייסין אז מיט גיטין וואלט מען אסאך מער גפועלט.

## English

Concerning the holy Tzaddik Reb Yitzchak Leib the Great, a disciple of Rabbainu — who had previously been a great performer of wonders, using practical Kabbalah, famous throughout the world for this. The holy Tzaddik Reb Nachum of Chernobyl heard of him, passed through his town on a journey, and caused him to fall into a great spiritual descent.

Rabbainu immediately traveled that same route and passed by Reb Yitzchak Leib. Rabbainu said to himself: "Aykuft yenm arop tsu vorfn? Aykuft yenm oyf tsi haybn!" [Should I throw him further down? I should lift him up!] Reb Yitzchak Leib prostrated himself before Rabbainu, begging to be received as a disciple. Rabbainu received him on condition that he perform no more wonders, and that throughout that year he travel with Rabbainu to all the places

That Tzaddik was a great ascetic who could not bear even the smell of a woman, and Reb Gershon would sleep in the same room with him. Reb Gershon had grown up from his earliest childhood in the home of the holy Tzaddik Reb Levi Yitzchak of Berdichev [and there is a full story to tell about this]. Reb Levi Yitzchak cherished Reb Gershon above all — he truly could not live without him. He and all the world said of Reb Gershon that he was a malach, an angel of Tzaddikim.

# יז)
## יז)
- Book: Stories from R Shmuel Horowitz
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/stories-סיפורים-מר--שמואל-הו/1/18

## English

When Rabbainu was traveling in concealment and hiddenness, once he came to some village before the morning prayer and requested a room to pray in. The householder understood this was a wondrous person, commanded his servant to prepare a meal for Rabbainu, and honored him greatly. During the meal the innkeeper poured out his troubles about his livelihood. Rabbainu replied: things will be good — only do not be a fool: "Nor a nar zolstu kayn nar nit zayn." Then he continued on his way.

Some days later a nobleman came to the inn, needed to relieve himself, went behind the inn — and forgot there his money-belt [beyya gortel] with sixty thousand gold coins. He drove on. # כא)
## כא)
- Book: Stories from R Shmuel Horowitz
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/stories-סיפורים-מר--שמואל-הו/1/22

## English

From Moharan'as: there was one of our fellowship in a village who held a lease. A certain German [gentile landlord] came and wanted to add to the terms and take the lease away from him. He came before Moharan'as with a great complaint. Moharan'as replied: "Vos vilstu ikh zol dariber ton? Nemen dem Daytsh? — vos hostu datsim Rabeyne shleper-Daytsh?" [What do you want me to do about it? Deal with the German? — what did Rabbainu have to do with a German?] "Rather: you beseech Hashem that he should not be able to harm you — and I too will help you in prayer for this." And so it was — through their prayer it was brought about that the German could not harm him and could not remove him from his lease.

## Hebrew

מר' נפתלי שהי' באו מן ומהרנ"ת נפטר בברסלב וידע תיכף מפטירתו וסיפר שבלילה ראה את מוהרנ"ת ז"ל ר"ל ושאל אותו "ר' נתן וויא לופט איהר" והשיב לו "איך לוף צום רעבין" והבין מזה שנפטר.

## English

Reb Shmuel Ayzik once saw Eliyahu the Prophet running. He asked him: "Where are you running?" He replied: "To the heart of the world." He asked: "Who is the heart of the world?" ## English

He was full of suffering from this — for he thought that at least after the toil and exhaustion of the entire day he would at least find rest at home at night — and in the end he found such "rest." He told his distress before Moharan'as — that he barely had his life from this.

# כט)
## כט)
- Book: Stories from R Shmuel Horowitz
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/stories-סיפורים-מר--שמואל-הו/1/30

## English

Just as one can observe: a person can sit in a shop all day and sell nothing — and when the designated time comes, in a quarter of an hour he earns for the entire period. And similarly in most cases, when one needs something and toils for it by the person one thinks can provide it — ultimately it does not work out at all, and the effort was wasted. And Hashem helps from a completely different direction that one never expected — and it would never have occurred to one that from there salvation could come. May Hashem save us speedily, kain yehi ratzon.

## English

In the morning Reb Volf arose from the wagon, harnessed his horses, and — the courtyard gates had already been opened [for in the morning when people are walking and traveling, the innkeeper had no power to detain a man or kill him, since the man could call out and the authorities would come] — he drove off with his wagon and escaped.

# לה)
## לה)
- Book: Stories from R Shmuel Horowitz
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/stories-סיפורים-מר--שמואל-הו/1/36

## English

Rabbainu said: "Shmirah in di hoyzn" [Guardianship within the trousers]. Concerning matzah — for which meticulous G-d-fearing people are careful to have shmirah [guarding from moisture] from the time of harvesting, and some are stringent from the time of grinding — Rabbainu said about this that the primary shmirah is to guard against the violation of the holy covenant — meaning: the mind, from evil imaginings and evil thoughts. For this is the primary chametz even in the minutest amount, as is explained in his holy books, in Likutay Tefilos, and in Likutay Halachos — that this is the primary chametz in a minute amount. May Hashem guard us from this, kain yehi ratzon.

## English

Rabbainu said Mashiach will have more work with the false famous Chassidim of lying leaders than with the free-thinkers and heretics — because the free-thinkers want to understand through wisdom, and Mashiach will show them through wisdom that the truth is with him, and they will acknowledge it. But the false Chassidim — who believe false beliefs — when Mashiach shows them the truth plainly, they will answer: "I believe!" "Ich glaub!" — even though they see clearly otherwise, they believe in falsehood despite reason. "Az Mashiach vet zey ausvayzn dem emes — veln zey zogn: 'Ich glaub' — khalil' ikh farsheyt nit azoy, glaybikh fort." May Hashem protect us, amen.

## English

Once someone asked one of our fellowship: "Tell us what you feel in Breslov Chassidus at your Rosh HaShanah." He answered: "Have you ever tasted an egg?" He answered yes. "Then describe for me the taste." This he could not describe — for it is not sweet, not sour, not bitter — one must taste it to know it. "So too with this: only when you taste it will you understand."

## English

Rabbainu said: "I envy Reb Yoskel" — regarding the simplicity called prastak, without cleverness or sophistication. This Reb Yoskel was a very simple person with a thick old siddur containing all the old techinos, yotzros, and additions. # ו)
## ו)
- Book: Stories from R Shmuel Horowitz
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/stories-סיפורים-מר--שמואל-הו/1/50

## English

Rabbainu said that to tell a jest [vertl] three conditions are required: first — it must not be coarse speech; second — it must not be said to demean one's fellow; third — it must not be said to praise oneself. "Eyns: es zol nit zayn nibl peh. Tsveytns: er zol nit eynem tsi trefn. Dritns: er zol zikh nit meynen." And Rabbainu concluded: "Now — say a jest!" "Na — zog shoyn a vertl!" Rabbainu also said: "There is nothing more crooked than a straight jest." "Nit a kayn krimers fun a gloykhm vertl."

# א)
## א)

## English

Reb Nachman of Tulchin told that he heard from Moharan'as who had heard from Rabbainu: what is stated in Likutay Moharan chapter 112 — that the discerning person should pray throughout all his days to merit even once in his entire life to speak one word of true speech as it should be before Hashem. And Rabbainu said: the essential true word emerges specifically in a descent — when things go against one, in the midst of obstacles and pressures — precisely then does one cry out a single word of truth. This explains the verse: "And Pharaoh brought close [va'yikrev]" — bringing the Jewish people to the point that "the children of Yisroel cried out to Hashem" — crying out a single word from the depths of the heart.

## English

Once on Pesach a question arose at Rabbainu's table — a piece of matzah had fallen into a cooked dish regarding the matter of not eating gebrokhts [matzah soaked in liquid]. He did not rule stringently about this, saying: "The primary shmirah is in the trousers!" "Shmirah in di hoyzn!" — meaning: the essential stringency is the guarding of the holy covenant. In this one must be very stringent. But in other matters, if it is kosher according to the Shulchan Aruch, one need not be overly stringent. And as our fellowship says, the letters of VaCHaY [and they shall live] stand for Velo Chumros Yeseiros [and not extra stringencies].

# א)
## א)
- Book: Stories from R Shmuel Horowitz
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/stories-סיפורים-מר--שמואל-הו/1/61

## English

They told before Rabbainu about the holy Tzaddik Reb Nachum of Chernobyl — that when the time for lighting the Chanukah candles arrived [the first night], he made a full body-height leap from the greatness of the holy light he was experiencing. Rabbainu said: "This is because he had not prepared himself sufficiently for this light beforehand — he had not prepared vessels to receive the light many days before." For Rabbainu himself would prepare with hisbodedus and preparation of vessels to receive the light — many days before each Yom Tov. Therefore even whatever light he experienced at the moment of candle-lighting — he would not leap, because he already had vessels ready to receive it. ## English

Moharan'as was once in a spiritual descent and was struggling and toiling to rise from it and illuminate himself. And meanwhile Reb Nachman of Tulchin came to him seeking spiritual sustenance. Moharan'as was agitated within: "I am struggling and toiling to illuminate myself — and now he comes and needs something from me? How can I help him?" Nonetheless Moharan'as restrained himself and said nothing to Reb Nachman. He reflected within: "Perhaps through my pressing myself to bring light to myself — through this very struggle I will make an opening to illuminate him and others as well." ## English

There was one of our fellowship who rose every night at midnight and toiled with himself to recite all of Tehillim. It came to him with great difficulty — yet despite this he completed all of Tehillim every night. And in his neighborhood there was a rabbi of the anti-Chassidic faction who said: "These two Breslov people" — meaning this man with his nightly Tehillim, and another one of our fellowship who toiled to study several pages of Gemara each day before the morning prayer — "these two absolutely do not allow me to remain an opponent of the Breslov people, for I am so deeply moved by them."

# ד)
## ד)
- Book: Stories from R Shmuel Horowitz
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/stories-סיפורים-מר--שמואל-הו/1/91

## English

Moharan'as said: "The world says: if one is going to eat pork — at least let it drip on the beard." "Az men est khazir — zol khatashe rinen iber der bord." [Meaning: since one is going to sin anyway, might as well sin fully so the pleasure is not wasted.] "But I say: if one is already eating pork — at least let it not drip on the beard." "Az men est shoyn khazir — zol khatashe nit rinen iber der bord." [Meaning: even when one sins, G-d forbid, at least do it minimally — for everything is reckoned in the great accounting, and even a slight lessening of the sin is of great weight.]

## Hebrew

פעם אחד בתחילת התקרבותו של ר' נפתלי לרבינו ז"ל הי' לו פעם אחד איזה ויכוח עם רבינו ז"ל שרבינו ז"ל אמר איזה דבר ור' נפתלי נתפלפל אתו ואמר שהוא רואה את הענין לא כן והשיב לו רבינו ז"ל הלא אינך רואה בטוב ותיכף נסתלק ממנו הר" נפתלי וסבל על העיניים והבין שזה עונש מרבינו ז"ל והתחיל בהשתדלות לבקש מרבינו ז"ל שיהי' לו רפואה על העיניים ואז כשהי' אצל רבינו ז"ל אמר לו רבינו ז"ל שילך להמנהל שלו ויקח זה הספר והוא יראה לו בתוך הספר כי כדבריו כן הוא ותיכף הלך ונתפתחו עיניו וראה ליקח הספר ורבינו הראה לו כנ"ל ואעפי"כ בסוף ימיו סבל על העיניים ורצה לעסוק ברפואות ומוהרנ"ת ז"ל כתב לו דברי תוכחה כי רבינו ז"ל כיוון בדברו (שהפליג לדבר על רפואות הרופאים) גם העיניים וכו' כמובא בעלים לתרופה:

# ה)
## ה)
- Book: Stories from R Shmuel Horowitz
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/stories-סיפורים-מר--שמואל-הו/1/92

## English

Rabbainu said: "When one is healthy, one must act and act and act" — in the service of G-d. "And when one becomes ill, G-d forbid — then there is nothing to do except to fulfill one mitzvah: veshamartim et nafshoteikhem [you shall guard your souls]." "Az men iz gezunt darf men ton un ton un ton — un az men vert khalile krank, hot men gor nit tsi ton, nor mekayem tsi zayn eyn mitzvah: veshamartim et nafshoteikhem." And the Ba'al Shem Tov said: "When a small hole occurs in the body, a large hole is made in the soul." And our fellowship said: the letters of VaCHaY [and they shall live] stand for Velo Chumros Yeseiros [and not extra stringencies].

# ו)
## ו)
- Book: Stories from R Shmuel Horowitz
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/stories-סיפורים-מר--שמואל-הו/1/93

## English

Reb Gershon of Vilednik of our fellowship said once that in Rabbainu's holy books, he never brings any matter without giving counsel for it — yet why does he bring at the end of Sefer HaMiddos the statement: "The thought only follows the one who serves G-d" — meaning: the intensification of improper thoughts comes precisely to one who serves Hashem — without giving any counsel for this at all? And the answer is that after this it is written in large letters: "CHAZAK" — as is customary to write at the end of a book. And this itself is the counsel: one must strengthen oneself. And this very knowledge — that such thoughts intensify specifically for one who serves G-d — is itself a great strengthening, so that one not fall from this but strengthen oneself against them.

## Hebrew

פעם אחד בא איזה עני בעירו של הגאון בעל חתם סופר ז"ל והי' אצל הגבאים של הביהמ"ד ונתנו לו פתקאות לאכול ימים (יום אחד אצל זה הבע"ב ויום אחד אצל זה הבעל הבית וכו') ועל שבת נתנו לו פתקא לאכול אצל החתם סופר ז"ל ולקח את הפתקא והלך עמה ברחוב ופגש את החתם סופר ז"ל (ולא ידע שזהו שצריך לאכול אצלו) ושאל אותו אם אצל זה האיש נותנים לאכול היטב. והשיב לו שאצל זה האיש נותנים לאכול דגים היטב. ואח"כ כשהי' אצלו על שבת לאכול אצלו (ולא הכירו שזה הוא שפגשו ברחוב ושאלו) והתחילו ליתן הדגים והוא חשב שיותר מהדגים לא יתנו ע"כ אכל א"ע הרבה עם הדגים ובפרט כי נתנו הרבה מנים מדגים וכו' ואח"כ כשהתחילו ליתן שאר תבשילים ומאכלים כבר לא הי' יכול לאכול כלל כי' הי' שבע והתחיל לכעוס ולקלל זה האיש שפגש וכו' ושאל אותו החתם סופר מה אתם כועסים וקוללים והשיב לו וסיפר לו המעשה שפגש איש ושאלו והשיב לו שנותנים דגים וע"כ אכל א"ע עם הדגים

# ח)
## ח)
- Book: Stories from R Shmuel Horowitz
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/stories-סיפורים-מר--שמואל-הו/1/95

## English

Reb Nachman of Tulchin — when guests were at his table for the Shabbos meal and they were singing zemiros, and the dish of food was brought to the table — he would say they should eat immediately, for the food will get cold and the zemiros will not get cold. "Dos esn vet kalt vern un di zemiros vet nit kalt vern." And furthermore, the food [of Shabbos] is Biblically mandated while zemiros are rabbinically mandated. And Reb Nachman of Tulchin would wipe the bowl with bread and eat it, saying that Rabbainu says the eating of Shabbos is entirely holy — as cited in Likutay Moharan in several places. Therefore a little extra holiness is also good.

## Hebrew

פעם אחד נסע הבעש"ט ז"ל דרך עיר אומן וסבבו אותו מחנות מחנות יונים והוא עמד את עצמו אצלם ואמר להם אני לא אוכל להשאיר אצלכם לתקן אתכם רק נכדי הוא יתקן אתכם וסבב להם בידיו שיכלו ממנו ופרחו ממנו. וכן מצאו פעם אחד קמיע של הרה"צ ר' נפתלי כ"ץ ז"ל שהי' כתוב שם לך ליער גרעקוב אצל עיר אומן ושם תמצא תיקונך".

# ג)
## ג)
- Book: Stories from R Shmuel Horowitz
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/stories-סיפורים-מר--שמואל-הו/1/99

## English

Reb Avraham had a dispute with Reb Michal of Tulchin, grandson of Moharan'as, on the matter of Eretz Yisroel versus Uman. Reb Michal said one must travel to Eretz Yisroel — but remain near Rabbainu and come to the holy grave each time. Reb Avraham said one must live in Eretz Yisroel and travel to Uman for Rosh HaShanah. Reb Michal said his greatest wish was that his grandchildren should be in the Diaspora and come to Uman for Rosh HaShanah. Reb Avraham replied: "Sona'ei Tsiyon zol azoy lebn — az ayre eynikelekh veln forn af Rosh HaShanah!" [May your enemies live like that — that your grandchildren should travel for Rosh HaShanah!] And so it was fulfilled — only a few travel rather than the many who should.

## Hebrew

The story of Chacham Yechezkel — a great Sephardic sage, a holy man of G-d, a great Tzaddik with a revelation of Eliyahu HaNavi — and the Sephardic sages of the generation came to him. Before the passing of Chacham Yechezkel there was an event: his lamp which he studied by went out. He kept going back to check whether it was burning — and he saw [a wondrous sign relating to his imminent passing]. There is also a beautiful story about Chacham Yechezkel who went with other Kohanim to the burial cave of Aharon HaKohen — but I do not remember it well enough to recount it properly.

## English

Reb Mikheli of Tulchin, grandson of Moharan'as, said regarding communal prayer and its great virtue — that it is accepted before Hashem even if there are inferior members of the congregation who do not pray properly — because the prayer of the entire community together transcends the level of the individual parts.

# ב)

## English

Reb Nachman, the grandson of Moharan'as, said: "Can we understand the mercy of Hashem?" — meaning: because these are the ways of Hashem which cannot be understood by human reasoning. The ways of Divine Providence are entirely beyond comprehension — and what seems to us like harshness is in reality infinite compassion.

## Hebrew

# ג)
## ג)
- Book: Stories from R Shmuel Horowitz
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/stories-סיפורים-מר--שמואל-הו/1/116

## English

Rabbainu told a story that the Ba'al Shem Tov had told — about a certain poritz [nobleman] who had a Jewish innkeeper who had held his lease for a long time. Afterward the poritz dealt with him in a way that appeared harsh — but was ultimately for the innkeeper's great benefit. The parable teaches: Hashem's seemingly difficult dealings with Yisroel are always for their ultimate good, and what seems like cruelty is always an act of infinite mercy.

## Hebrew

ר' אברהם ז"ל אמר לענין הציונים, הם תועים אבל תועים טוב לא"י. "זייא בלאנדיזין אבער זייא בלאנדזין גיט קיין ארץ ישראל". (והסוף והי' שיעשו תשובה).

Regarding the tradition from Rabbainu that Breslov Chassidim should not intermarry among themselves — once they wanted to make a match between Reb Noson and Reb Naftali. ## ב)
- Book: Stories from R Shmuel Horowitz
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/stories-סיפורים-מר--שמואל-הו/1/134

## English

There was one of our fellowship who rose every night at midnight and toiled with himself to recite all of Tehillim. It came to him with great difficulty — yet despite this he completed all of Tehillim every night. And in his neighborhood there was a rabbi of the anti-Chassidic faction who said: "These two Breslov people" — meaning this man with his nightly Tehillim, and another one of our fellowship who toiled to study several pages of Gemara each day before the morning prayer — "these two absolutely do not allow me to remain an opponent of the Breslov people, for I am so deeply moved by them."

# ד)

## English

Concerning Rabbainu's shofar: after Rabbainu passed away, the story was known that he had told of the arousal he experienced from the shofar he heard on the first day of Elul — and his daughter came to him that Shabbos and said: "Father — I too had a great awakening from the shofar-blowing today," as the story is told in Sichos HaRan. And Rabbainu said then the Torah teaching in Likutay Moharan chapter 141 which begins: "If one merits, one will feel the pain of one's sins" — and this Torah and the prayer upon it in Likutay Tefilos chapter 85 are connected to the month of Elul.

# ו)
## ו)
- Book: Stories from R Shmuel Horowitz
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/stories-סיפורים-מר--שמואל-הו/1/138

## English

Reb Noson wanted to tell Rabbainu his own dream — that he had been engaging with Rabbainu in the Torah of chapter ten. But before he could, Rabbainu said: "You do not need to tell me — I myself know, for you are the one who answered and said the proof from be'terua d'ika rucha." After this, Reb Noson took Rabbainu's shofar and would blow it himself the entire month of Elul — and only on Rosh HaShanah would he give the shofar to the community. And specifically Reb Meir Leib Blechir would blow on it. After Moharan'as's passing, Reb Yitzchak son of Moharan'as took the shofar — and when he traveled to the Holy Land he took it with him to Tzfas the holy city. And the shofar remained in Tzfas — and also Rabbainu's chalat [garment] and belt remained there.

## Hebrew

רבינו ז"ל אמר שבליל שבועות הוא העיקר התעוררות השינה שלא לישן כל הלילה ובהו"ר העיקר האמירה "שבועות איז דער עיקר דאס הוף זיין אין הושיתא רבא איז דער עיקר דאס זאגין".

# א)
## א)

- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/stories-סיפורים-מר--שמואל-הו/1/139

## English

Moharan'as would sit at the third Shabbos meal and say Torah to our fellowship with arousal — continuing until several hours into the night. And Yosil Beriz [who would beat himself with a birch-broom in the steam bath] — the father of Reb Moshe of Breslov — would enter after Ma'ariv with his pipe and sit comfortably, smoking his pipe with a calm and clear mind, and listening to Moharan'as's Torah at the third meal. And Moharan'as would say that he envied him [for the tranquility and comfort of his mind] — yet nonetheless did not want his mind: "Er iz im mekane zayn moykh iz im ruyik — nor viln mayn hobn zayn moykh vil er nit." [He envies him that his mind is calm — but to have his mind — that he does not want.]

And there is a story about Reb Pinchas of Kivlitz — how a certain slaughterer tore a page from one of Rabbainu's books and threw it into a privy. # ד)
## ד)
- Book: Stories from R Shmuel Horowitz
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/stories-סיפורים-מר--שמואל-הו/1/145

## English

Moharan'as said: "The world says: if one is going to eat pork — at least let it drip on the beard." "Az men est khazir — zol khatashe rinen iber der bord." [Meaning: since one is going to sin anyway, might as well sin fully so the pleasure is not wasted.] "But I say: if one is already eating pork — at least let it not drip on the beard." "Az men est shoyn khazir — zol khatashe nit rinen iber der bord." [Meaning: even when one sins, G-d forbid, at least do it minimally — for everything is reckoned in the great accounting, and even a slight lessening of the sin is of great weight.]

"וואס דער בעל דבר קען אין איין רגע קיין איך גיאנד ווערין אין זי"א שיין ווערין".

## English

Rabbainu said: "When one is healthy, one must act and act and act" — in the service of G-d. "And when one becomes ill, G-d forbid — then there is nothing to do except to fulfill one mitzvah: veshamartim et nafshoteikhem [you shall guard your souls]." "Az men iz gezunt darf men ton un ton un ton — un az men vert khalile krank, hot men gor nit tsi ton, nor mekayem tsi zayn eyn mitzvah: veshamartim et nafshoteikhem." And the Ba'al Shem Tov said: "When a small hole occurs in the body, a large hole is made in the soul." And our fellowship said: the letters of VaCHaY [and they shall live] stand for Velo Chumros Yeseiros [and not extra stringencies].

## English

# ח)
## ח)
- Book: Stories from R Shmuel Horowitz
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/stories-סיפורים-מר--שמואל-הו/1/149

## English

Reb Nachman of Tulchin — when guests were at his table for the Shabbos meal and they were singing zemiros, and the dish of food was brought to the table — he would say they should eat immediately, for the food will get cold and the zemiros will not get cold. "Dos esn vet kalt vern un di zemiros vet nit kalt vern." And furthermore, the food [of Shabbos] is Biblically mandated while zemiros are rabbinically mandated. And Reb Nachman of Tulchin would wipe the bowl with bread and eat it, saying that Rabbainu says the eating of Shabbos is entirely holy — as cited in Likutay Moharan in several places. Therefore a little extra holiness is also good.

# ד)
## ד)
- Book: Stories from R Shmuel Horowitz
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/stories-סיפורים-מר--שמואל-הו/1/153

## English

Reb Avraham had a dispute with Reb Michal of Tulchin, grandson of Moharan'as, on the matter of Eretz Yisroel versus Uman. Reb Michal said one must travel to Eretz Yisroel — but remain near Rabbainu and come to the holy grave each time. Reb Avraham said one must live in Eretz Yisroel and travel to Uman for Rosh HaShanah. Reb Michal said his greatest wish was that his grandchildren should be in the Diaspora and come to Uman for Rosh HaShanah. Reb Avraham replied: "Sona'ei Tsiyon zol azoy lebn — az ayre eynikelekh veln forn af Rosh HaShanah!" [May your enemies live like that — that your grandchildren should travel for Rosh HaShanah!] And so it was fulfilled — only a few travel rather than the many who should.

## Hebrew

## English

They told before Rabbainu about the holy Tzaddik of Volotishsk [who was Rabbainu's in-law] — that he said he had already been yearning and longing to ascend to Eretz Yisroel for forty years. And the holy Tzaddik of Khvilnik [also Rabbainu's in-law] said: "Why do they need to yearn so much? If they want to travel — just open the strongbox, take the money, and travel!" Rabbainu said: "This one will travel and arrive in Eretz Yisroel — and that one will not." For the primary thing is the will and the yearning.

## English

And once Rabbainu said: "The primary obstacle that is harder and heavier than all else is only the obstacle of the mind [and the heart]. For if there is no obstacle of the mind — meaning: if there is no doubt in the mind, and one is absolutely determined that one must do this particular thing, and the will is strong — then whatever other obstacles there may be: his wife, all the people in the world opposing him, or money, or the sea — all would be broken by the strong will." [As the world says: "Will breaks iron."] Therefore if one does not complete a thing with one's will, this is a sign one did not truly want it — for there is nothing that stands against a true will. ## English

Reb Natan's custom during the Three Weeks was to recite the kinos [lamentations] with tallis and tefillin. ## English

Reb Mikheli of Tulchin, grandson of Moharan'as, said about communal prayer and its great virtue: it is accepted even if there are inferior members in the prayer — just as when one gives several coins together, even if there is an inferior coin among them it still passes. But if one gives only a single coin, it is examined carefully. So it is with communal prayer versus individual prayer. And Reb Mikheli lived in Tulchin and was very distinguished. He would study Torah publicly there, and after the prayer would stand with the other ardent members of our fellowship and speak with them of matters of the service of G-d. ## English

Once there was a person of our fellowship who was at Moharan'as's home on Erev Shabbos. He heard and understood from the dispute between Moharan'as's wife and him that he had nothing at all for Shabbos. And this person had at his home five rubles that he needed for his own Shabbos. He went and brought the five rubles and gave them to Moharan'as that he should use them for the holy Shabbos. Meanwhile, past the window came a mentally deficient man walking barefoot — and his feet were full of wounds and blood, for it was the season of Tevet with snow and frost. Moharan'as called him into the house and asked him: "Why are you going barefoot — why don't you buy yourself shoes?" He answered: "Because I have no money." Moharan'as asked him if with five rubles he could buy shoes. He answered yes.

# א)
## א)
- Book: Stories from R Shmuel Horowitz
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/stories-סיפורים-מר--שמואל-הו/1/178

## English

Reb Moshe of Breslov, a disciple of Moharan'as, was praying Minchah on Erev Rosh HaShanah in the kloiz. Once when he began to say the Ketoret: "And Hashem spoke to Moshe, saying..." he fell faint and had to be revived for a long time. They asked him why he had fallen faint. He answered: he had begun "And Hashem spoke to Moshe" and had contemplated: Hashem spoke with Moshe — a person of flesh and blood! A person of flesh and blood can purify himself so much that Hashem speaks with him! And he was so aroused from this that he fell faint. # א)
## א)

## English

Rabbainu once saw young men who studied a great deal. He said to them: "If you were close to me you would study less — but more." "Ven ir zent tsi mir mekurev volt ir vintsikoyer gelernt ober shoyn mer gelernt." [For they would be studying lishmah — for its own sake — with holiness, purity, and awe, turning Torah teachings into prayers.] And similarly with the holy Tzaddik of Berdichev: his father-in-law said to him that since becoming a Chassid he studies less than before. He answered: "Before, I had to study a little for my father-in-law, a little for my mother-in-law, a little for my wife, and a little at least for Hashem too — so I had to study a great deal to have enough for all of them. But now that I study only for Hashem — however much I study is enough."

## English

In the days of Moharan'as, when conscriptions began, men would make themselves physically defective in order not to be taken for military service — some making themselves deaf and so forth, and some even blinding one of their eyes. ## English

At that same time of the military conscriptions, a woman had a son who was to be taken as a soldier. She went to the cemetery and wept so much that her soul departed from her. They told this before Moharan'as. He said: "What did she accomplish with this? She died — and she did not save her son. And she would also have saved many, many Jewish souls through this."
