## English

The Ramchal now opens the extended section on the FIVE SENSES — though the Zohar and Tikkunim generally mention only FOUR. And the secret: all worlds were created in the secret of ESSENCE and VESSELS. The Reshimu [the residual impression left after the Tzimtzum] = the VESSEL. And the Kav [line of Ayn Sof entering the space] = the LIGHT. The vessel is intrinsic in its limitation [for from it the infiniteness was removed]; the Kav is contingent in its limitation [for in itself it is infinite but accommodates itself to the Reshimu]. And the general sensitivity of the body = TOUCH [mishush] — this is the soul enclosed within the body in all parts, responsive to everything that touches the body. # Adir BaMurom — Chapter 16: The Name of Atik Yomin — Hidden in Torah; Revealed at the Akeidah; The Tzimtzum
## אדיר במרום — פרק 16
- Book: Adir BaMurom
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/ramchal-adir-bamuroam/1/16

## English

The Idra now says: "taana, shmeih de-atika satim mi-kola" — the name of Atik is hidden from all, and is not revealed in the Torah except in one place. The Ramchal opens here the most profound and exalted discussion of the entire Idra: the secret of creation itself, and how all of governance — the existence of the Sitra Achra, the exile, the Patriarchs, Moshe, and Mashiach — are all rooted in the two primordial acts of the blessed Emitter: the TZIMTZUM [contraction] and the EXTENSION OF THE KAV [line of Ayn Sof].
Before the renewal of existence there was only the Emitter — an Infinite, Undifferentiated Light [or pashut beli tachlis]. On this the mind may not investigate. Even to say "He willed" or "He thought" is impossible, for these words express actions of the limited sefirot that came a

- Book: Adir BaMurom
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/ramchal-adir-bamuroam/1/17

## English

The Ramchal now explains how the FOUR GREAT LIGHTS that emerge from the flaring of the nose against the Great Sea [the Dikna] correspond to the FOUR KINGDOMS OF DANIEL. And the overarching principle: the blessed Emitter did not wish merely to push the evil away — He wished to RECTIFY the klippa itself, so that all would be humbled and subjugated to holiness. This is done through the Shechina vesting herself within the four kingdoms during the exile — and in that process the good within them is extracted and bound to holiness's service, while the evil is eventually discarded.

## אדיר במרום — פרק 18
- Book: Adir BaMurom
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/ramchal-adir-bamuroam/1/18

## English

All the rectifications that human beings must make — all of which go toward eliminating the secret of Tohu and Vohu — all depend upon THIS RUACH. For: "the spirit of G-d hovered upon the face of the waters" — even in the hour when there was Tohu and Vohu, the Ruach of Mashiach never ceased hovering upon the face of the waters. Therefore it can afterward strengthen and become the light. And: even in exile, which is the aspect of Tohu and Vohu, this Ruach hovers. But at the time of redemption when it is revealed: "the people who walked in darkness have seen a great light" — as in: "and a spirit passed and cleared them" [Job 37:21].

- Book: Adir BaMurom
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/ramchal-adir-bamuroam/1/19

## English

When the MACHSHAVAH [Chochma/thought] goes out and emanates from Keter, each part of it that would arise to exit — instead of exiting — would cling upward, from below to above, to the RISHA [head/Keter] itself. And the lights of the Reshimu [the remnant of Keter] would roll and spin through this clinging and pursuit. And from this force a NEW LIGHT would be emanated within the Risha, from this very pursuit — not a light that the Risha itself would shine from its own side, but from the rolling of its lights through the pursuit, and from the cleaving of Machshavah itself in its pursuit of Risha. This generated light — born from the pursuit — would draw to itself, through the rolling of Risha's lights, what it could draw. And so all ten lights of Machshavah did. Two anchor-verses run through all eleven discourses:
Each of the eleven discourses reads both verses through a distinct kabbalistic lens. The four words of ascent — yarum, v'nisa, v'gavah, me'od — serve as a four-stage ladder, corresponding each time to a different set of four realities: four worlds, four kingdoms, four Partzufim, four levels of Torah, and so on.
The Ramchal's formula throughout: ורזא דא — "and the secret of this is" — signals that what follows is not mere identification but an unlocking of hidden meaning encoded in the verse.

## הקדמה
- Book: Tikunim Chadashim
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/ramchal-tikunim-chadashim/1/1

## English

TIKUNIM CHADASHIM
תיקונים חדשים
New Tikunim
by Rabbi Moshe Chaim Luzzatto (the Ramchal)
An Introduction to the Tikunim Chadashim
I. The Author
Rabbi Moshe Chaim Luzzatto (1707—1746), known by the acronym Ramchal, stands among the most extraordinary figures in the history of Jewish mysticism. Born in Padua to a distinguished family, he demonstrated prodigious gifts from childhood, mastering not only Talmud and Halachah but the full breadth of Kabbalistic literature — the Zohar, the writings of the Ari [Rabbi Yitzchak Luria], and the vast output of the Safed school — before reaching adulthood. He was also a master of Hebrew poetry, rhetoric, and philosophy, composing works that became cornerstones of musar literature, most famously the Mesilas Yesharim [Path of the Upright].

# Tikunim Chadashim - Tikun 1
## תיקון א
- Book: Tikunim Chadashim
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/ramchal-tikunim-chadashim/1/2

## English

ולכל היד החזקה ולכל המורא הגדול אשר עשה משה לעיני כל ישראל
"And for all the mighty hand and for all the great awe which Moshe did before the eyes of all Israel." [Devarim 34:12]

Theme: Love and Awe [Ahavah and Yirah] — inseparable; Moshe's charge to Israel; the Shechina nesting within the Tzaddik
I. Love and Awe — Bound Together
"The mighty hand" — this is Love [Ahavah]. "The great awe" — this is Awe [Yirah]. For there is no love without awe and no awe without love — they are bound one with the other and joined one with the other. The Hand — this is Love. "The mighty" — the Awe encompassed in it. "The Awe" — this is Yirah. "The great" — the Love encompassed in it. And one who has no love and awe is not fitting to come before the King. And Moshe warned Israel: "And now Israel, what does Hashem your G-d ask of you, but to fear...and to love" [Devarim 10:12].

ולכל היד החזקה ולכל המורא הגדול
"And for all the mighty hand and for all the great awe..." [Devarim 34:12]
Theme: The five Books of Torah and the אויר (Avir — Air/Light-Yud); the six orders of Mishnah; the Gemara; the supernal New Torah; difficulties [kushios] and Elijah's resolutions
I. The Five Alefs and the Five Vowels — The Five Books
"The mighty hand" — these are the five Books of the Torah — which are five times Ohr [light] of the Works of Creation. And here is a supernal hidden mystery above all — that hidden and unknown place, no color at all — called אויר (Avir — Air). What is Avir? — Ohr-Yud [Light + Yud]. For when matters began to expand, Ohr [light] emerged on one side and Yud on one side — and it became known that all was encompassed above in that Avir that cannot be grasped.

# Tikunim Chadashim - Tikun 31
## תיקון לא
- Book: Tikunim Chadashim
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/ramchal-tikunim-chadashim/1/32

## English

ולכל היד החזקה ולכל המורא הגדול אשר עשה משה לעיני כל ישראל
"And for all the mighty hand and for all the great awe which Moshe did before the eyes of all Israel." [Devarim 34:12]
I. The Covenant Renewed at the Redemption
"The mighty hand" — in the time of the redemption. For then the bonds [kitrin] will be renewed to bind the holy people to their roots as is fitting. And if you say — new bonds? — Not so; rather the renewal of the bonds. The mystery: the covenant He made with them when they went out of Egypt — and He will make with them again in the time to come. And this is the Mighty Hand — through which Israel were circumcised in Egypt to remove the foreskin from them. # Tikunim Chadashim - Tikun 46
## תיקון מו
- Book: Tikunim Chadashim
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/ramchal-tikunim-chadashim/1/47

## English

ולכל היד החזקה ולכל המורא הגדול אשר עשה משה לעיני כל ישראל
"And for all the mighty hand and for all the great awe which Moshe did before the eyes of all Israel." [Devarim 34:12]
I. The Shechina's Strength in Exile — Renewed in an Instant
"The mighty hand" — this is the strength of the Shechina. For in exile She was weak. # Tikunim Chadashim - Tikun 63
## תיקון סג
- Book: Tikunim Chadashim
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/ramchal-tikunim-chadashim/1/64

## English

ולכל היד החזקה ולכל המורא הגדול אשר עשה משה לעיני כל ישראל
"And for all the mighty hand and for all the great awe which Moshe did before the eyes of all Israel." [Devarim 34:12]
Moshe Gives Power to Receive Reward; Standing Before Supernal Courage
"The mighty hand" — this is Moshe who is destined to come to give strength to the righteous to receive their reward. For the gates are opened wide — and many blessings go out freely into the world — and they need to be prepared and available to receive them. "The great awe" — for they will be able to stand in that supernal courage through which the angels are guided. For of human beings it is said: "do not enter into judgment with Your servant" [Tehillim 143:2]. But at that time — they will be so established that they will be able to stand in it.

# Tikunim Chadashim - Biur (Commentary)
## ביאור הרמח"ל
- Book: Tikunim Chadashim
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/ramchal-tikunim-chadashim/1/72

## English

ביאור על קטע מהאידרא מתוך אגרת של רבינו הרמח״ל
BIUR — EXPLANATION OF A PASSAGE FROM THE IDRA
From a Private Letter of Our Master the Ramchal of Blessed Memory
I. Preamble — The Novum of the Ramchal’s Idra; The Question about Tikun One
And now I shall record for him a small matter from the Idra — and from it he will see that all that is said in it is a novum [chiddush] — that which is not revealed in the words of Rashbi of blessed memory — even though it is possible that it is alluded to in his words in a concealed manner. The words of the Idra are as follows:
[Tikun One]: “these are the three El-s that stand there — and it has been stated — in which three worlds are rooted...” Note: in his saying “and it has been stated” — one sees that he is alluding to what appears in the Idra of Rashbi

## English

The Unification of Awe
A Kabbalistic Treatise on the Inner Meaning of Yiras Haromimus
Translator's Introduction
"Behold for you this great and awesome Yichud — guard it and remember it, for it is your life."
"Strengthen yourselves and be courageous in the sincere service [of God] and in the Torah of our God, and in the true love that we have taught ourselves in our study-house — and the Awe of Sublimity in which we have walked: let it not depart from you. Know and see that God has no desire in His world except that His servants should recognize His honor, and exalt His greatness, and rejoice in His hidden places."
I. The Author and His World

## חלק א: היחוד
- Book: Yichud HaYeeruh
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/ramchal-yichud-hayeeruh/1/2

## English

Yichud HaYeeruh
The Unification of Awe
A Treatise by Rabbi Moshe Chaim Luzzatto (Ramchal) Translated with commentary & notes Segment 1 of 3: Introduction & The Yichud Text (Sections א–טו)
Segment 1 · Pesach Devorim & The Yichud · Sections א–טו
פתח דברי — Opening of Words (Editor's Introduction)
Among the collected writings of our great master the Ramchal1 — Rabbi Moshe Chaim Luzzatto — there is found the awesome treatise "Yichud HaYeeruh" יחוד היראה — "The Unification of Awe" — in which are expounded great and lofty secrets concerning yir'as haromimus יראת הרוממות — Awe of the [Divine] Sublimity — and its [spiritual] effect and operation. The treatise is found in two manuscripts: the Columbia University manuscript (Ms. X 893 K 17) and the Mantua manuscript (Ms. 112 2). Both are copies made

The Order of the Chain-Descent and Extension of Matters from Atik to Nukva
I will now complete the elucidation of the order of all these matters — how they chain-descend and extend — and afterwards I will explain the effect and the consequence of each. Behold:
The lights of Atik — you have already heard that their secret is אהיה אשר אהיה, and from their striking emerge the four letters of אדנ"י etc. Afterwards, in Chochma Stima'ah [Concealed Wisdom], the lights of Awe and Wisdom blaze as described above, and one existence is emanated whose secret is Da'as [Knowledge] — and this is the clear Knowledge [yedi'ah brurah]. - Book: Otzros Ramchal
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/ramchal-otzros-ramchal/1/1

## English

Otzros Ramchal
Part One — Commentaries on Torah & Nach
Contents — This Volume
Bereishis
"In the beginning G-d created the heavens and the earth…" | [Genesis 1:1–5]
Elokim is the Sefira that brings forth Zu"n [Zeir Anpin and Nukva — the "masculine" and "feminine" aspects of divinity in the supernal realm] — "the heavens and the earth." Therefore it says "bara" (created), for Ima [the Divine Mother — the Sefira of Bina, identified with Elokim] dwells and nests within the act of creation.
The Sages taught: the word את (es) comes to include their offspring. They likewise taught that among the things that preceded the creation of the world is the Name of Mashiach. On this basis we may say that this verse speaks of Melech HaMashiach — the King Messiah. It is known that Mashiach ben Dovid has his

# Mattos-Masei through Vezos HaBeracha
## מטות-מסעי — וזאת הברכה
- Book: Otzros Ramchal
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/ramchal-otzros-ramchal/1/4

## English

Volume IV
Contents
Mattos
"And Moshe spoke to the heads of the tribes…" | [Numbers 30:2]
The reason this mitzvah is connected to the heads of the tribes: because they stand in the dimension of mochin (divine intellect). For whoever holds any position of authority receives from the head — and therefore they are called "heads of the tribes." And now Moshe needed to command the mitzvah of vows (nedarim), which is a particular rectification within the mochin. As the Sages said: whoever makes a vow is as if he vowed by the life of the King. Therefore He commanded this mitzvah to them. MS A

- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/ramchal-otzros-ramchal/1/5

## English

Volume V
Contents
Shmuel Alef
"And Chana rose after eating in Shilo and after drinking — and Eli the Kohen was sitting upon the seat by the doorpost of the Sanctuary of Hashem." | [I Samuel 1:9–20]
Chana is the Shechina, as we know. "After eating in Shilo" — because she dwells in synagogues and houses of study where Israel study. And the Torah is the "eating" — as it says: "for it is your life and the length of your days." "Shilo" refers to synagogues and houses of study. "Eating" — although the Shechina does not literally eat, she reflects what Israel does. Therefore it says "eating" even though she does not eat.
And Eli the Kohen is the Holy One, Blessed is He. He is called "Eli" because the Shechina is called ya'al (ascend), and the Holy One — Eli (my height). And he is the High Kohen.

Iyov — Conclusion of the Leviathan Teaching
"The pride of his shields is closed — with a tight seal." | [Job 41:7 — conclusion]
Know that the secret of "pride" (ga'ava) is the revelation of the light in all its parts — and this is its boasting. And behold — when the channels of divine influence which are in the dimension of Yesod enter and channel into the Yesod of Nukva — and this is when Yesod enters into Malchus and is hidden within it — "closed." And the Yesod of Nukva is the seal made from Ima. And also "narrow" (tzar) which is peh-resh — the five Gevuros of mem-nun-tzaddik-peh-chaf. And this is the pride of Yesod — to be sealed within the tight seal. [Yaakov] MS A

# Maamar HaVikuach (The Discourse of the Debate)
## מאמר הויכוח
- Book: Shaaray Ramchal
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/ramchal-shaaray-ramchal/1/2

## English

מַאֲמַר הַוִּכּוּחַ
חֵלֶק רִאשׁוֹן
The First Discourse
Refutation of the Philosopher's objections against the truth and benefit of Chochmas HaEmes
§1Philosopher: Peace be upon you, my brother! How good is your arrival at this time, for I am greatly in need of you.
§2Kabbalist: How would a philosopher have need of a Kabbalist? You have already roamed your thought over every corner of Creation and subdued it beneath you with your decisive proofs — so what benefit could I bring you?
§3Philosopher: Excessive flattery is nothing but a snare. But let us come to the desired matter. I shall speak with you in the honesty of my heart, as befits our friendship. I have read and heard certain matters from your Kabbalah, and they appeared to me as something utterly foreign — for they are entirely contra

Introduction to Pischay Chochmah VaDaas
By R' Chaim Friedlander z"l
One who studies the books of our great master, the man of G-d, Rabbi Moshe Chaim Luzzatto z"tzal, and other books that engage with Chochmas HaEmes — finds before him, at the beginning of his study, many concepts that are new to him, each with many particulars. # Aitzoas HaMivoo'aroas — Chapters 4, 5 & 6
- Book: Aitzoas HaMivooaroas
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/aitzoas-hamivooaroas/1/10

## English

— Translator's Summary —
This brief but pointed chapter presents the commandment of hospitality — specifically, hosting genuine Torah scholars — as a spiritual remedy with two powerful effects. First (§1): it breaks heretical views and the influence of false teachers, granting the host the strength to stand firm against opponents of truth. Second (§2): it rectifies one's prayer life — purging "bad prayers" born of lust and material desire — and elevates one's requests to Hashem to the level of genuine, true prayer.
The cross-references to "Eating" §§10 and 19 underscore that hospitality, kashruth, and prayer are all facets of one spiritual system. The Zoharic phrase "Jewish demons" for false scholars is preserved exactly as written, as it appears in the original text.
— Translator's Summar

These two letters, written from Uman — the resting place of Rebbe Nachman of Breslov — introduce us to Rabbi Shimshon Barski as a deeply devoted Breslov Chassid, serving as a spiritual mentor and guide to a circle of Anash based in Lublin.

# Gevooroas Shimshon — Letters 3–7 (Corrected)
- Book: Gevuros Shimshon
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/gevuros-shimshon/1/2

## English

The following errors in the first edition have been corrected in this version:
1. Torah portion in Letter 3's header was labeled Vayigash — corrected to Vayechi (Bereishis 49:2).
2. All instances of וכו׳ (etc.) — previously dropped silently — are now rendered as [וכו׳] throughout, preserving Rabbi Shimshon's deliberate use of this convention to signal an intentional omission or trailing thought.
3. The double repetition תכלית התכלית in Letter 3 — "the ultimate purpose, the ultimate purpose" — is now preserved with a translator's note marking it as deliberate.
4. The double repetition להשיב להשיב in Letter 5 — "to answer, to answer" — is now preserved with a translator's note.
5. The dateline of Letter 5 was headed "Tuesday" — corrected to Friday (the letter explicitly says erev Shabbos kod

# Gevooroas Shimshon — Letters 8–12
- Book: Gevuros Shimshon
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/gevuros-shimshon/1/3

## English

Letter 8 offers crucial spiritual comfort to Yitzchak Meir, who has written of intensified opposition to their sacred work. Rabbi Shimshon's response is electrifying: the very fact that the Baal Davar is raging so fiercely is itself proof that the work is bearing fruit — citing Likutay Moharan 22 on how every arousal of holiness generates a corresponding arousal of opposition. He also gives practical communal guidance on who should partner with whom in the outreach work, careful to keep those tainted by earlier strife separate.
Letter 9 is brief but pointed, sent near Passover. Its single urgent message: establish a fixed study session with a partner — for upon this depends the healing and renewal of the soul. And not study for its own sake alone — but to draw out from every subject clear,

# Gevooroas Shimshon — Letters 13–17
- Book: Gevuros Shimshon
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/gevuros-shimshon/1/4

## English

Letter 13 is brief but sweeping in scope. Rabbi Shimshon declares that the confusion and destruction among the Lublin fellowship cannot be fixed by human intelligence — it is too subtle, too spiritual. The repair depends entirely on the power of Rebbe Nachman, whose quality is netzach, netzach, v'yinatzeiach — eternal victory. And notably: the rectification needed among Anash themselves is far harder than the rectification of the entire world — because upon it depends the gemar hatikun, the completion of the cosmic repair.
Letter 14 is one of the most psychologically penetrating letters of the collection. Rabbi Shimshon diagnoses Yitzchak Meir's inner state from afar — smallness of mind, weakness of daas, faintness of spirit — all caused by the community's hidden jealousy and resentment. H

- Book: Gevuros Shimshon
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/gevuros-shimshon/1/5

## English

Letter 18 is written entirely in Yiddish — the only letter in this collection addressed to Avraham Dovid rather than Yitzchak Meir. It is a complete and practical guide to Breslov service: study the Rebbe's books like a Shulchan Aruch — extracting one clear practical law from every passage. Then pray and do hisbodidus every day, even for just a few minutes. Rabbi Shimshon's credential here is powerful: he says his counsel comes not from faith without knowledge, but from personal, lived clarification through his own trials and battles over many years.

# Gevooroas Shimshon — Letters 24–31
- Book: Gevuros Shimshon
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/gevuros-shimshon/1/6

## English

Letter 24 is a brief but important letter centered on the commandment of maaser — tithing one's income for charity. Rabbi Shimshon's counsel to his son Nosson: give the tenth even when your income seems scarce, for this is the teaching of the Sages, and the books of the Rebbe confirm that maaser is a propitious segulah for ample livelihood. He also cites Likutay Moharan Part 2 on the teaching of "G-d Almighty give you mercy" — one should not demand good according to one's own logic, but simply trust that all is for the good.
Letter 25 is very brief — a fragment — reporting that there is nothing new regarding livelihood, that G-d performs great miracles, but that great mercy is still needed. Pure trust is the only counsel.

# Gevooroas Shimshon — Letters 32–47
- Book: Gevuros Shimshon
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/gevuros-shimshon/1/7

## English

These sixteen letters span five years of Rabbi Shimshon's correspondence with his son Nosson. They form a remarkable unified tapestry of pastoral guidance — covering the same core themes repeatedly, yet always with fresh nuance and personal depth. The reader senses a father watching over his son from afar, with limited means of communication, patiently repeating the same essential medicines of the soul across the years.
The great recurring themes:
"In my distress You have broadened me" (Tehillim 4:2) — cited in Letters 34, 37, 42, and 47 — becomes the master-verse of this entire period. Rabbi Shimshon applies it as Rebbe Nachman's teaching: always look for the expansions and kindnesses even in times of constriction.

# Gevooroas Shimshon — Letters 48–65 (Final)
- Book: Gevuros Shimshon
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/gevuros-shimshon/1/8

## English

Letter 48 is a remarkable public circular — the only letter in the entire collection addressed to all Anash everywhere, not to an individual. Rabbi Shimshon sets out in full his theology of the Likutay Aitzos with Yiddish commentary. Two key teachings: (1) The Rebbe's main intention was always for the "dwellers below" — the lowest and simplest souls — so said Reb Nosson several times. (2) Without the Rebbe's daas, even a person called "Breslov Chassid" for years who travels to Uman has no substance in his drawing-close — citing Likutay Moharan 255 directly.

## אזמרה
- Book: Azamra / Rabbi Nachman: Who He Was
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/azamra/1/4

## English

(Likutay Nanach, see also the first footnote in the Afterword)
Likutay Moharan
A Collection [of Teachings of] Our Leader and Rabbi,
Rabbi Nachman
Know that it is necessary to judge every person favorably[1], and even someone who is completely wicked, it is necessary to search and find in him some bit of good, which in that bit he is not wicked, and through this that he finds in him a bit of good and judges him favorably, through this he raises him in truth to the favorable, and he (the onlooker) can return him in repentance.
And this is the aspect of (Psalms 37:10), “And a bit more and there is no wicked person, and you will contemplate on his place, and he is not there.” That is, that the verse exhorts to judge everyone favorably, and even though you see that he is completely wicked, even

# Azamra / Rabbi Nachman: Who He Was - Part 5
## אזמרה
- Book: Azamra / Rabbi Nachman: Who He Was
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/azamra/1/5

## English

Na Nach Nachma Nachman MayUman
Outpouring of the Soul
No matter how fallen, find some good point
When a person begins to look upon himself, and he sees that he is distant from being good, and that he is full of transgressions, then it is possible that through this he will fall, and will not be able to pray and do hisbodidus whatsoever. Therefore, he must search, and seek, and find in himself some good, for how is it possible that never in his life he did some mitzva or something good. And even though when he begins to look at that good which he did, he sees that the good itself is full of wounds, for the good is mixed with ulterior intentions and a lot of rot, even still, how is it possible that there will not be in the little good some good point. And so he should search and seek further,

# Azamra / Rabbi Nachman: Who He Was - Part 7
## אזמרה
- Book: Azamra / Rabbi Nachman: Who He Was
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/azamra/1/7

## English

Another important point concerning the way of Azamru, specifically when it is applied to oneself, is pointed out by Rabbi Nussun[18] and quoted in the holy book Aitzoas Hamivoa-aroas <The Explained Remedies> (Hischazkus-encouragement, article 19), that this way can be likened to the Red Heifer[19] which purifies those impure of contamination of the dead, but makes impure those who are pure[20], he does not elaborate but it can readily be understood, that if one turns a blind eye to his faults, and satisfies himself with some little good he has, this would be very destructive. Thus one must be extremely diligent and on guard to only utilize the method of Azamru to extract oneself and keep oneself out of the dark realm of sadness and evil, and to build on the good, but as he rises he must co

# Azamra / Rabbi Nachman: Who He Was - Part 8
## אזמרה
- Book: Azamra / Rabbi Nachman: Who He Was
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/azamra/1/8

## English

The Ramchal (Daas Tevunos II, published in Ginzay Ramchal) explains further, that in reality the soul of each Jew is a point of holiness rooted in the Torah and G-d (as the Arizal already made clear, that the 600,000 souls of Israel are rooted in the 600,000 letters of the Torah), just that they are disconnected and separated from their root, and sin and all types of evil can accumulate and encompass the soul until it is totally alienated from its source, and completely unrecognizable. Therefore, the main rectification is simply to give strength to the good point which is the person’s root and real essence, and all the evils which had taken hold of the soul will become foreign and fall away.
These are his words:
61. The Neshama (soul) said: That the sinner himself should be rectified by pu

## English

In the future when all the nations will recognize The Name (G-d) (as it says in Tsifanya 3) and everyone will believe in the Blessed G-d, there will be a fulfillment of the verse (Shir Hashirim – Song of Songs) “come sing from the height of faith,” specifically from the “height of faith” the aspect of the highest faith mentioned above, which is the head (root or source) of all faith as previously explained. This is why the verse says “sing” specifically, it is the tune and the melody associated with this height of faith mentioned above.
The aspect of melody of this exalted faith, no one merits except the Tzadik (holy sage) of the generation, who is an aspect of Moshe (Moses), who is on the level of this faith.

## English

Here, in this Torah-lesson Rabbi Nachman is revealing a new construct and practice of judging favorably, that is, even when there is no excuse for a person's conduct, one must not judge the person at all by that bad which he did, rather one must judge the person by some favorable point he has.
Elsewhere, Rabbi Nachman himself uses the standard understanding of judging favorable, e.g. in Character – The Aleph Bet Book of the Traits, Rabbi Nachman says it is forbidden to judge a wicked person favorably and one who does so is wicked, and that it is forbidden to judge homosexuality favorably, that is referring to trying to find justification for the persons conduct, to that end Rabbi Nachman warns that in certain cases it is forbidden to do so, whereas here Rabbi Nachman made it very clear, in

# Fires of Israel
## אשי ישראל
- Book: Fires of Israel
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/fires-of-israel/1/1

## English

The Fires of Israel
Memoirs of Saba Yisroel
R' Yisroel Dov/Ber Odesser o.b.m.
This book is comprised of 11 recordings of Saba Yisroel, from Sunday 21, Monday 22, & Wednesday 24 Elul 5741 (20-23 September 1981), in Jerusalem. Most of the conversation was in Yiddish with people who were counted among the Breslov Chasidim. These talks therefore have a different style and ambiance than most of the previously published ones which were said to an open public audience, or to neophytes, or just very close attendants. They go more in to depth about what Breslov was and what it should be in practice and ideology. They are replete with amazing insights, recollections, guidance, and weltanschauung from the unfathomable heart and soul of Saba Yisroel.
Na Nach Nachma Nachman MeUman
Please guard the sanc

# Introduction
## התבודדות
- Book: Hisbodidus - Alone Time
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/hisbodidus-alone-time/1/3

## English

Rabbi Nachman said (Life of Our Leader Rabbi Nachman, article 107) that in his youth, every time he would return from doing hisbodidus the world looked completely new. This is also an aspect of mastery, because the heightened understanding gained over the world, is new acquisition and secures dominion over it in an even more elevated state (of the world).[16]
There were many great tzadikim who helped elevate their brethren, these tzadikim would imbue those they came in contact with or prayed for, with such holiness that they would uproot them from whatever evils they were caught up in, and immediately bring them to a holy paradigm of existence. Rabbi Nachman reserved such treatment for rectifying the souls of the dead, but for those still living he almost never circumvented their personal

# Hisbodidus is a gateway to the Secrets of the Torah
## התבודדות
- Book: Hisbodidus - Alone Time
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/hisbodidus-alone-time/1/4

## English

One who wants to taste a taste of the ohr haganuz [cached light], that is, the secrets of the Torah that will be revealed in the future, he should abound in hisbodidus between himself and his Creator, and judge and adjudicate himself all the time, regarding all his affairs and conduct, if this is proper and befitting for him to do, and to conduct like this against Hashem Yisburach, Who deals out to him goodness all the time and at every instance. And he should “manage his affairs {/dispense his words} judicially (Psalms 112:5),” and bring himself to account for everything. He himself should judge and adjudicate himself over all his affairs and deeds, and by this, he will remove from himself all fright, and he will be saved from the fallen fears, meaning that he'll not be afraid or frighten

# Personal words to G-d are Divinely inspired
## התבודדות
- Book: Hisbodidus - Alone Time
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/hisbodidus-alone-time/1/5

## English

The words that a person converses and speaks between himself and his Maker are the aspect of ruach hakodesh (Divine inspiration), for through undertaking this, and forcing himself, and preparing himself to speak before Hashem Yisburach, Hashem Yisburach sends him words in his mouth which are the aspect of ruach hakodesh (Divine inspiration). And it is necessary to see to it, and to endeavor to innovate always, to beseech at all times with new words of appeasement and entreaties, and one merits this through purity of the heart, which one merits through the holy motion of the intellect (as is explained in the entry of Daas, article 3).
(Likutay Moharan, Torah 21 and 156. Outpouring of the Soul 64)

For through the longing alone, potential souls are made [because the yearning is the soul, in the aspect of (Psalms 84:3), “my soul yearns and pines (-even to the extent of expiration),” (added from Outpouring of the Soul)] and through the speaking mentioned above, they are completed and produced from potential (bikoach) to actuality (bifoal) [in the aspect of (Genesis 2:7), “and the man became a

# Connect the heart to its point to save it from the shame of fallen desires
## התבודדות
- Book: Hisbodidus - Alone Time
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/hisbodidus-alone-time/1/7

## English

In every Israelite there is an extremely precious good point, whose desire is always strong, to do the desire of its Maker, but the (worldly) desires break his heart, and through this his heart is distant from the point. Therefore it is necessary for every person to speak between himself and his Maker, in order to light up the aspect of the point which is in his heart, and through this his uncircumcised heart will be nullified, that is, the bad loves (-affections) which are the heart's disgrace, which break a person's heart [in the aspect of (Psalms 69:21), “disgrace broke my heart” (added from Outpouring of the Soul)]. [See the entry of Tzadik, article 42].
(Likutay Moharan 34:7-8; Outpouring of the Soul 57)
Na Nach Nachma Nachman MayUman

For until now he threw his sins behind his shoulders (-turned his back on them) and did not pay attention to them, and now that he acknowledges them, in this way he is inoculated with great embarrassment over the severity of his sins against a master and ruler, the essence and root of all the worlds, and this embarrassment is revealed on his face, and this shame is the aspect of the light of the tefillin, which

# Abnegation to be included in one’s root
## התבודדות
- Book: Hisbodidus - Alone Time
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/hisbodidus-alone-time/1/9

## English

It is necessary for every one to see to it that he is included in his root. And in order to be included in his root, it is necessary for him to have abnegation (“bitool”). And it is impossible to come to abnegation except through hisbodidus, because through seclusion of himself with his Creator, through this he can abnegate everything, and bind (“divaikus”) with Hashem Yisburach, and be included in his root.
(Likutay Moharan 52; Outpouring of the Soul 59)

# Hisbodidus at night, crying to G-d and building ones good points from out of the bad, bring joy, and holds lust at bay, and cultivates a consciousness of the future world
## התבודדות
- Book: Hisbodidus - Alone Time
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/hisbodidus-alone-time/1/11

## English

At night, then it is the main time for hisbodidus, that is to seclude oneself with his Creator, to express one's words before Hashem Yisburach, to converse with one’s heart[20] to seek out the good spirit, that is, the good points that he still retains, to cull them from within the bad spirit, until he pours out his heart like water directly before the countenance of Hashem (Lamentations 2:19), and through this he will merit to joy and to quell the imagination, from which all the desires ensue. And through this he will merit memory, to always remember the World to Come, and to think at all times of his purpose and ultimate end, of the World to Come, until he merits to truthfully return to Him blessed He.
(Likutay Moharan, Torah 54; Outpouring of the Soul 60).

# Sighing – to regain one's standing
## התבודדות
- Book: Hisbodidus - Alone Time
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/hisbodidus-alone-time/1/12

## English

When a person prays with divaikus (binding, clinging to Gd) or does hisbodidus properly, and in the middle he falls from his level, this stems from defection of (the) faith, and so it is necessary then to break his heart inside, and to be ashamed of himself for falling from heaven to earth, and he should pity himself until he sighs, and through the sigh he will return to his level.
(Likutay Moharan, torah 108; Outpouring of the Soul 63)
Na Nach Nachma Nachman MayUman

# G-d helps and provides words for one to prevail and be victorious despite all
## התבודדות
- Book: Hisbodidus - Alone Time
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/hisbodidus-alone-time/1/13

## English

When one speaks before the Holy One Blessed He and expresses his words with argumentations and supplications, and desires to best the Holy One Blessed He, so to speak, that He should do his bidding, the Holy One Blessed He derives exquisite pleasure and joy from this, that they are defeating Him. Therefore He Blessed He, Himself sends him words in his mouth, so that he can defeat Him, because otherwise it would certainly be impossible for (man of) flesh and blood to defeat the Holy One Blessed he, just, Hashem Yisburach Himself helps him with this, as mentioned above.
(Likutay Moharan 124; Outpouring of the Soul 24)

# Candidly unburdening oneself to G-d evokes Divine consolation
## התבודדות
- Book: Hisbodidus - Alone Time
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/hisbodidus-alone-time/1/14

## English

When a person does hisbodidus and expresses his words and his pain before Hashem Yisburach, and confesses and regrets the severity of the defects he impaired, then the Shechina (Divine Presence) directly across him expresses before him Her words and pain, for every single infraction and infringement that he violated in his neshama (soul), he inflicted by Her, so to speak, and She consoles him, that he should seek contrivances to rectify all the damages.
(Likutay Moharan, torah 259; Outpouring of the Soul 66)

## English

It is very good to pray and to express one’s words (-sentiments) before Hashem Yisburach in a field in the grasses and the trees. Because when a person prays and expresses his words in a field, then all the grasses and all the vegetation of the field, all of them come into his prayer and help him and give him power in his prayer and conversing.
(Likutay Moharan II, Torah 11; Outpouring of the Soul 27-8)

# Trying to cry is also a distraction
## התבודדות
- Book: Hisbodidus - Alone Time
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/hisbodidus-alone-time/1/18

## English

Even though crying before Hashem Yisburach with entreaties and beseeching is extremely good, even still, when a person says Psalms or other entreaties and supplications, or converses personally with his Creator, and he thinks and anticipates, and looks mindfully all the time that he should cry and shed tears, this also is a (distracting) foreign thought, and confuses the kavana (-concentration, intention). Because the main thing is – that he should concentrate his mind to say the words truly with all his heart, that he should incline his ear and his heart to hear what he is expressing with his mouth, and if he is aroused to cry, how wonderful – and if not, he should not confuse his concentrations for this.
(Likutay Moharan II, Torah 95; Outpouring of the Soul 3)
Na Nach Nachma Nachman MayU

# Hisbodidus is the only way to succeed
## התבודדות
- Book: Hisbodidus - Alone Time
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/hisbodidus-alone-time/1/19

# Hisbodidus Versus Meditation
## התבודדות
- Book: Hisbodidus - Alone Time
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/hisbodidus-alone-time/1/40

## English

Hisbodidus literally means to be alone in seclusion. The definition for meditation is: Continuous and profound contemplation or musing on a subject or series of subjects of a deep or abstruse or spiritual nature. The parameters of each of these disciplines can be broadened so that they overlap. Rabbi Aryeh Kaplan o.b.m., a great genius and prolific author and translator whose main mentor was a Breslover Chusid, wrote that probably his biggest chiddush (novel idea and insight) was to translate the common word “kavana” which people always use to mean focus of concentration and meaningful intention, as meditation. In this vein he went on to explain that hisbodidus can also be referring to meditation.

- Book: Seder HaYom (Daily Order)
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/breiter-seder-hayom/1/1

## English

At the onset of night one should say: "Behold, I desire to serve Hashem Yisborach in truth, in faith, and in joy — and I hereby bind all my thoughts, speech and actions of the entire day to all the true Tzaddikim of our generation, and to all the true Tzaddikim who dwell in the dust — the holy ones who are in the earth — and in particular to our holy master, the Nachal Novea Mekor Chochmah, Rabbainu Nachman son of Feiga, of blessed memory." And before every prayer one should say: "Behold, I bind my prayer to the true Tzaddikim."

---

# Ma'ariv — the Evening Prayer
## תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית
- Book: Seder HaYom (Daily Order)
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/breiter-seder-hayom/1/2

## English

One should pray with deliberateness, with strength, with kavvanah, with joy, and with a pleasant voice. One should be precise in pronouncing the cholam vowel when saying the holy Name of Hashem Yisborach — and one should also stress the yud in "Adonai." All the holy Names should be said with awe. For through this prayer all harsh judgments are sweetened, and one merits to strengthen oneself — to stand against all the descents and darknesses and obstacles that pass over every person — in the aspect of "He who guards His people Israel forever."

---

# Shema Before Sleep
## קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע שֶׁעַל הַמִּטָּה
- Book: Seder HaYom (Daily Order)
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/breiter-seder-hayom/1/3

## English

One should recite it with deliberateness and joy as above. Through this, one rectifies all the spiritual blemishes of the entire day — including all blemishes of the holy covenant, Rachmana litzlan — in the aspect of: "One who recites the Shema upon his bed — harmful spirits flee from him."

---

# The Accounting of the Soul
## מָארֵי דְחוּשְׁבָּנָא
- Book: Seder HaYom (Daily Order)
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/breiter-seder-hayom/1/4

## English

One should give thanks to Hashem Yisborach for all the good one merited to do that day, and confess all one's blemishes of speech and deed, and beseech Hashem Yisborach for forgiveness, pardon, and atonement — and that He help one from this time forward to be as He desires.

---

# Tikkun Chatzos — Midnight Rising
## חֲצוֹת לַיְלָה
- Book: Seder HaYom (Daily Order)
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/breiter-seder-hayom/1/5

## English

One should arise and mourn greatly over the destruction of the Holy Temple — over the concealment of the light of the true Tzaddik — and over one's sins, iniquities, transgressions, evil traits and evil desires that delay the rebuilding of the Temple. One should find oneself within everything that passes over one during the recitation of Tikkun Chatzos, and beseech Hashem Yisborach for the redemption and salvation of all Yisroel — and also for the redemption of one's own soul from the evil inclination that always lies in wait. The time of midnight always begins six hours after the emergence of the stars, and its period extends for two hours.

---

# Remembrance of the World to Come
## זִכָּרוֹן בְּעָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי
- Book: Seder HaYom (Daily Order)
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/breiter-seder-hayom/1/6

## English

When one awakens from sleep one should say Modeh Ani, and immediately remember the World to Come. One should pray to Hashem Yisborach that He help one to conduct oneself throughout the entire day in holiness, and renew the binding to the Tzaddik as at the onset of night described above.

---

# Rising Early
## הַשְׁכָּמָה
- Book: Seder HaYom (Daily Order)
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/breiter-seder-hayom/1/7

## English

One should rouse oneself to arise before dawn to engage in the service of Hashem Yisborach. Through this one merits completeness of faith — and the light of truth and great da'as shines upon one — and one merits to enter all the gates of holiness. At the light of morning one should raise one's eyes heavenward and gaze upon the sky.

---

# Preparation for Prayer
## הֲכָנוֹת הַתְּפִלָּה
- Book: Seder HaYom (Daily Order)
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/breiter-seder-hayom/1/8

## English

One should not eat, drink, or speak before prayer. Even essential speech should be as brief as possible — and through this one's prayer will be acceptable. For one must invest all one's strength and kavvanah in the words of prayer — and therefore one must not weaken or interrupt the yearnings of the soul that longs to pour out its speech before its Creator.

---

# Mikveh — Daily Immersion
## מִקְוֶה
- Book: Seder HaYom (Daily Order)
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/breiter-seder-hayom/1/9

## English

One should immerse oneself every single day. Through this one becomes sanctified and emerges from all the spiritual impurity of one's sins, and draws close to Hashem Yisborach in truth — and is saved from all troubles, both physical and spiritual — in the aspect of: "The mikveh of Yisroel is Hashem, Who saves in time of trouble."

---

# Shacharis — the Morning Prayer
## שַׁחֲרִית
- Book: Seder HaYom (Daily Order)
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/breiter-seder-hayom/1/10

## English

One should pray early in the morning with deliberateness as above. One should not interrupt with speech from the beginning of prayer until its end. One should pray from a siddur and not look here and there. One should answer Amen, Yehei Shemei Rabba, Barchu, and Kedushah with all one's strength, kavvanah, and joy as above. Through this one merits to illuminate upon oneself and upon all the world the light of the seven days — which is renewed each day — in the aspect of: "A new light upon Tzion may You shine, and may we all speedily merit its radiance."

---

# Shulchan Aruch — Daily Halachah Study
## שֻׁלְחָן עָרוּךְ
- Book: Seder HaYom (Daily Order)
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/breiter-seder-hayom/1/11

## English

One should study each day a fixed portion and not let a single day pass — all the days of one's life — without studying at least a little in the Shulchan Aruch. Through this one nullifies all manner of spiritual and physical heresy and strife from oneself and from all the world. One should study the Shulchan Aruch in order from beginning to end, and thus conduct oneself all the days of one's life. If one is unable to study the full Shulchan Aruch, one should study at least from the abridged codes — and in the same order described.

---

One should tell of one's pain and pressures and situation — and of one's household — and of all Yisroel. One should broaden the speech and plead with all manner of arguments, entreaties, and appeals, that one merit to draw close to Hashem Yisborach in truth — in the aspect of: "Open wide your mouth and I will fill it." - Book: Seder HaYom (Daily Order)

## English

# Fixed Times of Torah Study
## שִׁעוּרִים קְבוּעִים
- Book: Seder HaYom (Daily Order)
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/breiter-seder-hayom/1/16

## English

One should fix set times for Torah study and study with joy — not interrupting one's learning for anything not absolutely necessary. One should intend through the learning to merit complete faith, and strive to draw from the learning correct guidance for the service of Hashem Yisborach. One should also innovate in Torah — according to the foundations of the da'as of Rabbainu — and through this one draws close to Hashem Yisborach in truth and brings those far away near to the service of Hashem Yisborach.

---

# Eating
## אֲכִילָה
- Book: Seder HaYom (Daily Order)
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/breiter-seder-hayom/1/17

## English

One should eat with deliberateness and proper conduct — not becoming angry and not speaking unnecessary words at that time. One should study at one's table, and recite Birkas HaMazon with joy as above. Through this one draws down upon oneself the illumination of will — that is, longing and good desires to walk in the ways of Hashem. And so with all one's pleasures and activities — one should intend that it all be as He desires — so that there be a unification of the Holy Blessed One and His Shechina through one's eating, pleasures, and deeds.

---

# Business and Work
## מַשָּׂא וּמַתָּן אוֹ מְלָאכָה
- Book: Seder HaYom (Daily Order)
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/breiter-seder-hayom/1/18

## English

To act in faithfulness: one merits this through strengthening oneself in the faith of individual divine Providence — and through knowing and believing that one's livelihood does not derive through the natural course of circumstances, but only through the will of the Creator. Hashem Yisborach can sustain a person with no intermediary causes whatsoever. The reason Hashem provides a person's sustenance through causes is in order to test him — whether he will stand in the trials that arise through his engagement with those circumstances — and to discern whether he can maintain the faith that sustenance depends not on the circumstances but on the will of the Creator.

---

# Tzedakah — Charity
## צְדָקָה
- Book: Seder HaYom (Daily Order)
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/breiter-seder-hayom/1/19

## English

From every form of abundance that flows to one — by whatever means it comes — one should set aside tzedakah to support all the affairs of Rabbainu, including: sustaining the descendants and relatives of the Tzaddik who engage in the service of Hashem; printing and distributing his holy books throughout Yisroel at greatly reduced cost; and supporting his batei midrash. It is good to begin by setting aside at minimum a terumah — that is, two percent of one's income — until one merits to tithe all one's possessions fully.

---

Therefore this work must be for those close to the Tzaddik a Kodesh Kodoshim — they must engage in it with all their powers for its own sake — and at every opportunity seek counsel on how to expand it and spread his springs outward, to revive and restore the soul of all Yisroel to their Father in Heaven.

# Teshuvah — Return to G-d

To those who curse one or who demean one's soul — one should be silent and still. Through this one subdues the evil in one's blood, and all one's iniquities are atoned and transformed into merits.

# Love of Friends

## English

One should love all of Yisroel — and in particular those drawn close to the true Tzaddik — as one's own soul. One should speak with them every day about the ultimate truth, in order to receive from their good point — for in every one of Yisroel there is a good point that is not found in another.

# Minchah — the Afternoon Prayer
## מִנְחָה
- Book: Seder HaYom (Daily Order)
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/breiter-seder-hayom/1/25

## English

# Rosh HaShanah
## רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
- Book: Seder HaYom (Daily Order)
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/breiter-seder-hayom/1/26

## English

All those drawn close to the true Tzaddik must gather together in one place for Rosh HaShanah and pray in binding to the Tzaddik. Through this they receive from him a wondrous illumination — a rectification and great closeness — such as they cannot merit to obtain throughout the entire year. As Rabbainu said: "All my matters are Rosh HaShanah." Through this they merit to illuminate upon themselves and upon the entire world the light of the Tzaddik for generations upon generations. Therefore one must break through all obstacles of livelihood and money, of busyness and honor, and the like — and come to the gathering for Rosh HaShanah.

---

# Eretz Yisroel
## אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
- Book: Seder HaYom (Daily Order)
- URL: https://ajew.org/reader/breiter-seder-hayom/1/27

## English

All the days of one's life one should yearn, pray, and strive to settle in Eretz Yisroel — and at the very least to walk four cubits upon her soil. Through this one merits length of patience and the ability to ascend from level to level — and draws down upon oneself the totality of holiness. This is the essential victory of holiness for a person in this world. May Hashem Yisborach help us to walk in the ways of the true Tzaddik in truth and in faith — and to draw his light upon us and upon all Yisroel — and through this may we merit the redemption of body and soul, speedily in our days, Amen and Amen.
